sentences.zh: 馬永，字天錫，遷安人。

translations.literal: Ma Yong, styled Tiansi, was a native of Qian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yong, styled Tiansi, came from Qian'an.

sentences.zh: 生而魁岸，驍果有謀。

translations.literal: From birth he was tall and imposing, bold and resolute, and possessed of stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and imposing from youth, bold and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 習兵法，好《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: He studied military arts and delighted in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He studied warfare and loved the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 嗣世職為金吾左衛指揮使。

translations.literal: He inherited the hereditary post as commander of the Left Gold Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to the hereditary office of commander of the Left Gold Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 正德時，從陸完擊賊有功，進都指揮同知。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign he followed Lu Wan in attacking bandits with merit and was promoted to vice regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he served under Lu Wan against bandits with distinction and was promoted to vice regional commander.

sentences.zh: 江彬練兵西內，永當隸彬，稱疾避之。

translations.literal: Jiang Bin drilled troops in the Western Inner Palace; Yong was to be placed under Bin's command, but he claimed illness to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Bin drilled troops in the Western Inner Palace, Yong was ordered to serve under him, but he pleaded illness to stay clear.

sentences.zh: 守備遵化，寇入馬蘭峪，參將陳乾被劾，擢永代。

translations.literal: As garrison commander at Zunhua, when raiders entered Malan Pass, Assistant Commander Chen Qian was impeached and Yong was elevated to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: While defending Zunhua, he was promoted to replace Assistant Commander Chen Qian, who was impeached after raiders entered Malan Pass.

sentences.zh: 戰柏崖、白羊峪，皆有功。

translations.literal: In battles at Baiya and Baiyang Pass he achieved merit in both.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in fighting at Baiya and Baiyang passes.

sentences.zh: 十三年進都督僉事，充總兵官，鎮守薊州。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was advanced to junior regional commander, appointed regional commander-in-chief, and stationed at Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was made junior regional commander and regional commander-in-chief at Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 盡汰諸營老弱，聽其農賈，取備直給健卒，由是永所將獨雄於諸鎮。

translations.literal: He dismissed all the old and weak from the camps, allowed them to farm or trade, took their stipends to pay stout soldiers, and thereby the troops Yong led alone stood foremost among the garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared every camp of the old and weak, let them farm or trade, and used their pay to equip hardy troops; the force under his command alone outmatched the other garrisons.

sentences.zh: 武宗至喜峰口，欲出塞，永叩馬諫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong reached Xifeng Pass and wished to go beyond the border, Yong seized his horse's bridle and remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong reached Xifeng Pass intending to ride beyond the border, Yong caught his bridle and pleaded against it.

sentences.zh: 帝註視久之，笑而止。

translations.literal: The emperor gazed at him a long while, then laughed and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stared at him a long moment, then laughed and gave up the plan.

sentences.zh: 中路擦崖當敵沖，無城堡，耕牧者輒被掠。

translations.literal: On the middle route, Cayai faced the enemy's main thrust; there were no forts, and farmers and herdsmen were repeatedly plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Cayai on the middle route lay in the enemy's path with no fortifications, and farmers and herdsmen were raided again and again.

sentences.zh: 永令人持一月糧，營崖表，版築其內。

translations.literal: Yong had men carry a month's grain, encamp on the cliff face, and build ramparts within.
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent men up with a month's provisions to camp on the cliff and build walls behind them.

sentences.zh: 城廨如期立，乃遷軍守之。

translations.literal: The walled offices were raised on schedule, and he then moved the army to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: The fort rose on schedule, and he shifted the garrison to hold it.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進署都督同知。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was advanced to acting regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: His service was recognized and he was promoted to acting regional commander.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年，金山礦盜作亂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing, bandits rose at the Jinshan mines.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiajing, mine bandits rebelled at Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 遣指揮康雄討平之，塞其礦。

translations.literal: He dispatched Commander Kang Xiong to suppress and pacify them and sealed the mines.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Commander Kang Xiong to put down the revolt and closed the mines.

sentences.zh: 朵顏把兒孫結諸部邀賞不得，盜邊。

translations.literal: Ba'ersun of the Tümed, having rallied various tribes to demand rewards without success, raided the border.
translations.idiomatic: Ba'ersun of the Tümed, having mustered allied tribes for rewards in vain, turned to border raiding.

sentences.zh: 永迎擊洪山口，而伏兵斷其後，斬獲過當，進右都督。

translations.literal: Yong met them at Hongshan Pass while ambush troops cut off their rear; kills and captures exceeded the enemy dead, and he was advanced to right regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yong met them at Hongshan Pass while ambushers cut their retreat; the tally of heads and captives exceeded the enemy force, and he was made right regional commander.

sentences.zh: 已，復馘其驍將，把兒孫不敢復擾邊。

translations.literal: Later he again beheaded their fierce general, and Ba'ersun did not dare trouble the border again.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he slew another of their best fighters, and Ba'ersun never raided the border again.

sentences.zh: 大同兵變，殺巡撫張文錦，命桂勇為總兵官往鎮，而議將撫之。

translations.literal: The Datong troops mutinied and killed Grand Coordinator Zhang Wenjin; Gui Yong was ordered as regional commander to go and pacify the post, while the court debated whether to appease them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Datong garrison mutinied and killed Grand Coordinator Zhang Wenjin, Gui Yong was sent as regional commander while some at court argued for conciliation.

sentences.zh: 永言：「逆賊幹紀，朝廷赦其脅從，恩至渥也，顧猶抗命。

translations.literal: Yong said: "The rebels have violated discipline; the court has pardoned those coerced, with grace most ample, yet they still defy orders.
translations.idiomatic: Yong argued: "These rebels have broken the law. The court already pardoned those who were coerced—a mercy as broad as could be—yet they still resist.

sentences.zh: 今不剿，春和北寇南牧，叛卒勾連，禍滋大。

translations.literal: If we do not suppress them now, when northern enemies drive south in spring, the mutineers will link with them and the calamity will grow.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not strike now, northern enemies will drive south in spring and the mutineers will join them—the disaster will only widen.

sentences.zh: 宜亟調鄰鎮兵，克期攻城，曉譬利害，懸破格之賞，令賊自相斬為功，元兇不難殄也。」

translations.literal: We should urgently mobilize troops from neighboring garrisons, fix a day to assault the city, explain advantage and harm, offer extraordinary rewards, and have the rebels cut one another down for merit—the ringleaders would not be hard to exterminate."
translations.idiomatic: We should call in neighboring garrisons at once, set a date to storm the city, explain the stakes, offer extraordinary bounties, and let the rebels earn credit by killing one another—the ringleaders would fall easily."

sentences.zh: 乃命永督諸軍與侍郎胡瓚往。

translations.literal: He was then ordered to supervise the armies and go with Vice Minister Hu Zan.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Yong to take command and march with Vice Minister Hu Zan.

sentences.zh: 會亂平，乃還鎮。

translations.literal: The rebellion happened to be pacified, and he returned to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The revolt was already settled by the time he arrived, and he returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 永上書為陸完請恤典，且乞宥議禮獲罪諸臣。

translations.literal: Yong memorialized to request posthumous honors for Lu Wan and also begged pardon for the officials punished in the Rites Controversy.
translations.idiomatic: Yong petitioned for posthumous honors for Lu Wan and for clemency toward the officials condemned in the Rites Controversy.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，奪永官，寄祿南京後府。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, stripped Yong of his office, and retained his salary at the Nanjing Rear Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, stripped Yong of rank, and kept him on salary at the Nanjing Rear Palace.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史丘養浩言：「永仁以恤軍，廉以律已，固邊防，卻強敵，軍民安堵，資彼長城。

translations.literal: Investigating censor Qiu Yanghao said: "Yong is benevolent in comforting the troops, frugal in restraining himself, firm in border defense, and repelling strong enemies; soldiers and civilians live in peace and rely on him as their long wall.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Qiu Yanghao wrote: "Yong is humane toward his men, strict with himself, steadfast on the frontier, and formidable against strong foes. Soldiers and civilians live in peace because they lean on him like a long wall.

sentences.zh: 聞永去，遮道乞留，且攜子女欲遂逃移。

translations.literal: Hearing that Yong was leaving, they blocked the road begging him to stay, and even carried their children intending to flee altogether.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard Yong was leaving, they blocked the road to beg him to stay, some packing up their families to flee with him.

sentences.zh: 夫陸完久死炎瘴，非有權勢可托。

translations.literal: Lu Wan has long been dead in the miasmal south and has no power to be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wan has long been dead in the southern wilds; he holds no power anyone could lean on.

sentences.zh: 永徒感國士知，欲救區區之報。

translations.literal: Yong merely felt gratitude for a patron's recognition and wished to repay a trifling debt.
translations.idiomatic: Yong acted only from gratitude to a patron and wished to repay a small debt of honor.

sentences.zh: 不負知己，寧負國家？

translations.literal: Would he fail a confidant rather than fail the state?
translations.idiomatic: Would he betray a friend rather than betray the realm?

sentences.zh: 祈曲賜優容，俾還鎮。」

translations.literal: I pray you graciously grant indulgence and allow him to return to his garrison."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty's gracious indulgence to let him return to his command."

sentences.zh: 順天巡撫劉澤及給事、御史交章救之，俱被譴。

translations.literal: Shuntian grand coordinator Liu Ze and supervising secretaries and censors submitted successive memorials in his defense, and all were rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Shuntian grand coordinator Liu Ze joined supervising secretaries and censors in pleading for him, and all were censured.

sentences.zh: 永竟廢不用。

translations.literal: Yong was ultimately dismissed and not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was never restored to office.

sentences.zh: 永杜門讀書，清約如寒士。

translations.literal: Yong shut his doors to read books, living in plain frugality like a poor scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Yong withdrew to his books and lived as plainly as a poor scholar.

sentences.zh: 久之，用薦僉書南京前府。

translations.literal: After a long while, on recommendation he was appointed to assist in the Nanjing Front Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Years later, on recommendation, he was appointed assistant in the Nanjing Front Palace.

sentences.zh: 大同軍再亂，廷臣交薦。

translations.literal: When the Datong army rebelled again, court officials recommended him in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Datong mutinied again, officials at court urged his recall in one memorial after another.

sentences.zh: 召至，已就撫，復還南京。

translations.literal: He was summoned, but pacification was already achieved, and he returned again to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned, but the revolt was already settled, and he went back to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遼東兵變。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the Liaodong troops mutinied.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the Liaodong garrison mutinied.

sentences.zh: 罷總兵官劉淮，以永代之。

translations.literal: Regional commander Liu Huai was dismissed and Yong replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Liu Huai was removed and Yong took his place.

sentences.zh: 大清堡守將徐顥誘殺泰寧衛九人。

translations.literal: The defending commander at Daqing Fort, Xu Hao, lured and killed nine men of the Taining Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Hao, defender of Daqing Fort, tricked and killed nine men of the Taining Guard.

sentences.zh: 部長把當孩怒，寇邊，永擊斬之。

translations.literal: The tribal chief Badanghai was enraged, raided the border, and Yong attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The chief Badanghai raided in anger; Yong struck and killed him.

sentences.zh: 其族屬把孫借朵顏兵報讎，復為永所卻。

translations.literal: His kinsman Basun borrowed Tümed troops to avenge him and was again repelled by Yong.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Basun borrowed Tümed troops for revenge and was driven off again.

sentences.zh: 已，復入犯。

translations.literal: Later they invaded again.
translations.idiomatic: They raided again not long after.

sentences.zh: 中官王永戰敗，永坐戴罪。

translations.literal: The eunuch Wang Yong was defeated in battle, and Yong was punished by bearing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Wang Yong was defeated, Yong was sentenced to serve with a demerit on his record.

sentences.zh: 遼東自軍變後，首惡雖誅，漏綱者眾。

translations.literal: Since the Liaodong mutiny, although the ringleaders were executed, many who escaped the net remained.
translations.idiomatic: After the Liaodong mutiny the ringleaders were killed, but many accomplices remained at large.

sentences.zh: 悍卒無所憚，結黨叫呼，動懷不逞。

translations.literal: Fierce soldiers feared nothing, formed factions and shouted, and were ever ready for mischief.
translations.idiomatic: Hardened troops feared nothing, banded together in uproar, and were always ripe for trouble.

sentences.zh: 廣寧卒佟伏、張鑒等乘旱饑，倡眾為亂，諸營軍憚永無應者。

translations.literal: Guangning soldiers Tong Fu, Zhang Jian, and others, taking advantage of drought and famine, incited the masses to revolt; troops in the various camps feared Yong and none responded.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangning, Tong Fu, Zhang Jian, and others exploited drought and famine to stir a revolt, but troops in the other camps feared Yong and would not join.

sentences.zh: 伏等登譙樓，鳴鼓大噪，永率家眾仰攻。

translations.literal: Fu and the rest mounted the watchtower, beat drums and raised a great clamor; Yong led his household retainers in an upward assault.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's band seized the watchtower, beat drums, and roared; Yong led his household guard in an assault up the tower.

sentences.zh: 千戶張斌被殺，永戰益力，盡殲之。

translations.literal: Thousand-commander Zhang Bin was killed; Yong fought all the harder and annihilated them completely.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-commander Zhang Bin fell in the fight, but Yong fought harder still and wiped them out to the last man.

sentences.zh: 事聞，進左都督。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was advanced to left regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was promoted to left regional commander.

sentences.zh: 永畜士百余人，皆西北健兒，驍勇敢戰。

translations.literal: Yong kept more than a hundred warriors, all hardy youths of the northwest, fierce and bold in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yong kept more than a hundred retainers, northwestern hardmen who fought with exceptional courage.

sentences.zh: 遼東變初定，帝問將於李時。

translations.literal: When the Liaodong disturbance was first settled, the emperor asked Li Shi for a general.
translations.idiomatic: As the Liaodong crisis was settling, the emperor asked Grand Secretary Li Shi whom to send.

sentences.zh: 時薦永，且曰：「其家眾足用也。」

translations.literal: Shi recommended Yong and said: "His household retainers are sufficient for use."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi recommended Yong and added, "His household guard alone would suffice."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「將須文武兼，寧專恃勇乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "A general must combine civil and military arts—can one rely on courage alone?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "A commander needs both civil and martial gifts. Can courage alone suffice?"

sentences.zh: 時曰：「遼土新定，須有威力者鎮之。」

translations.literal: Shi said: "Liaodong has just been pacified and needs a man of imposing force to hold it."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi answered, "Liaodong has only just been pacified. It needs a man of overwhelming force to hold it."

sentences.zh: 至是，竟得其力。

translations.literal: By this time he indeed obtained his strength.
translations.idiomatic: In the event, that judgment proved exactly right.

sentences.zh: 都御史王廷相言：「永善用兵，且廉潔，宜仍用之薊鎮，作京師藩屏。」

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Wang Tingxiang said: "Yong is skilled in employing troops and moreover honest and clean; he should again be used at the Jizhou garrison as a screen for the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Wang Tingxiang urged: "Yong commands troops well and is incorruptible. He should return to Jizhou as a shield for the capital."

sentences.zh: 未及調，卒。

translations.literal: Before he could be transferred, Yong died.
translations.idiomatic: Before the transfer could be made, he died.

sentences.zh: 遼人為罷市。

translations.literal: The people of Liaodong closed the markets in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Liaodong shut their markets in mourning.

sentences.zh: 喪過蘇州，州人亦灑泣。

translations.literal: When the funeral procession passed Suzhou, the townspeople also wept as they sprinkled tears.
translations.idiomatic: When his funeral train passed Suzhou, townspeople wept along the road.

sentences.zh: 兩鎮並立祠。

translations.literal: Both garrisons jointly erected shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Both garrisons raised shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 永為將，厚撫間諜，得敵人情偽，故戰輒勝。

translations.literal: As a general Yong generously supported spies and obtained the enemy's true and false reports, and therefore he prevailed whenever he fought.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander Yong paid his spies well and learned the enemy's true intentions, which is why he seldom lost a battle.

sentences.zh: 雅知人，所拔卒校，後多至大帥。

translations.literal: He excelled at knowing men; the camp officers he promoted later mostly rose to great command.
translations.idiomatic: He had a gift for spotting talent; many officers he promoted later became leading generals.

sentences.zh: 尚書鄭曉稱永與梁震有古良將風。

translations.literal: Minister Zheng Xiao said that Yong and Liang Zhen had the air of ancient worthy generals.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zheng Xiao said Yong and Liang Zhen bore the spirit of the great generals of old.

sentences.zh: 梁震，新野人。

translations.literal: Liang Zhen was a native of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zhen came from Xinye.

sentences.zh: 襲榆林衛指揮使。

translations.literal: He inherited the post of commander of the Yulin Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to command of the Yulin Guard.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖七年進署都指揮僉事，協守寧夏興武營。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiajing he was advanced to acting junior regional commander and assisted in defending the Xingwu camp in Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiajing he became acting junior regional commander and helped defend the Xingwu camp in Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 尋充延綏遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed mobile corps general of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made mobile corps general on the Yan-sui front.

sentences.zh: 廉勇，好讀兵書，善訓士，力挽強命中，數先登。

translations.literal: Honest and brave, he loved reading military books, was skilled in training troops, could draw a strong bow with unerring aim, and often was first to scale the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and fearless, he studied military texts, drilled his men hard, shot powerfully and accurately, and often led the assault.

sentences.zh: 擢延綏副總兵。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice regional commander of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice regional commander on the Yan-sui front.

sentences.zh: 與總兵官王效卻敵鎮遠關，進都督僉事。

translations.literal: Together with regional commander Wang Xiao he repelled the enemy at Zhenyuan Pass and was advanced to junior regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: With regional commander Wang Xiao he drove the enemy from Zhenyuan Pass and was made junior regional commander.

sentences.zh: 吉囊、俺答犯延綏，震敗之黃甫川。

translations.literal: Jinong and Altan invaded Yan-sui; Zhen defeated them at Huangfu River.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinong and Altan raided Yan-sui, Zhen defeated them at Huangfu River.

sentences.zh: 尋犯響水、波羅，參將任傑大敗之。

translations.literal: Soon they invaded Xiangshui and Boluo; Assistant Commander Ren Jie inflicted a great defeat on them.
translations.idiomatic: They struck again at Xiangshui and Boluo, where Assistant Commander Ren Jie routed them.

sentences.zh: 吉囊復以十萬騎入寇，震大破之幹溝，獲首功百余。

translations.literal: Jinong again entered with a hundred thousand horsemen; Zhen routed them at Gangan Ravine and took more than a hundred heads for merit.
translations.idiomatic: Jinong returned with a hundred thousand horsemen; Zhen shattered them at Gangan Ravine and claimed more than a hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 先後被獎賚。

translations.literal: He was rewarded and bestowed gifts in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He received repeated imperial rewards.

sentences.zh: 已，增俸一等。

translations.literal: Later his salary was increased by one grade.
translations.idiomatic: His salary was later raised one grade.

sentences.zh: 幹溝凡三十里，當敵沖。

translations.literal: Gangan Ravine extended thirty li in all and lay in the enemy's path.
translations.idiomatic: Gangan Ravine ran thirty li along the enemy's main route.

sentences.zh: 震浚使深廣，築土墻其上，寇不復輕犯。

translations.literal: Zhen had it dredged deep and wide and built earthen walls atop it; raiders no longer ventured to violate it lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen deepened and widened the ravine and raised earthen walls along it, and raiders no longer crossed it lightly.

sentences.zh: 十四年進都督同知，充陜西總兵官。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was advanced to regional commander and appointed regional commander-in-chief of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he became regional commander and regional commander-in-chief of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 尋論黃甫川功，進右都督。

translations.literal: Soon, in recognition of merit at Huangfu River, he was advanced to right regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his victory at Huangfu River won him promotion to right regional commander.

sentences.zh: 明年移鎮大同。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to command at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Datong.

sentences.zh: 大同亂兵連殺巡撫張文錦、總兵官李瑾。

translations.literal: Datong's mutinous troops had in succession killed Grand Coordinator Zhang Wenjin and Regional Commander Li Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Datong's mutineers had already killed Grand Coordinator Zhang Wenjin and Regional Commander Li Jin in turn.

sentences.zh: 繼瑾者魯綱，威不振，兵益驕，文武大吏不敢要束。

translations.literal: Lu Gang succeeded Jin, but his authority did not revive; the troops grew ever more arrogant, and civil and military grand officers did not dare restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Gang succeeded Li Jin, but his authority never took hold; the troops grew bolder still, and neither civil nor military superiors dared discipline them.

sentences.zh: 廷議以為憂，移震往。

translations.literal: The court regarded it with alarm and transferred Zhen there.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed at the situation, the court sent Zhen to Datong.

sentences.zh: 震素畜健兒五百人，至則下令軍中，申約束。

translations.literal: Zhen had long kept five hundred hardy warriors; on arrival he issued orders throughout the army and proclaimed discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had long maintained five hundred tough fighters; as soon as he arrived he laid down strict discipline throughout the army.

sentences.zh: 鎮兵素憚震，由是帖服。

translations.literal: The garrison troops had always feared Zhen, and thereby became submissive.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison had always feared him, and now fell into line.

sentences.zh: 寇入犯，震破之牛心山，斬級百余。

translations.literal: When raiders invaded, Zhen defeated them at Niuxin Mountain and took more than a hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders struck, he routed them at Niuxin Mountain with more than a hundred kills.

sentences.zh: 寇慎，駐近邊伺隙。

translations.literal: The raiders grew cautious and camped near the border watching for an opening.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy grew wary and lingered near the frontier, watching for a chance.

sentences.zh: 時車駕祀山陵，震伏將士於諸路。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial carriage was sacrificing at the imperial tombs; Zhen concealed troops along the various routes.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was at the tombs for sacrifice, Zhen posted troops along every approach.

sentences.zh: 寇果入，大破之宣寧灣，又破之紅崖兒，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: The raiders did enter; he routed them at Xuannig Bay and again at Hongyai'er, with very many killed and captured.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders came as expected; he crushed them at Xuannig Bay and again at Hongyai'er, taking a great toll in heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 進左都督，蔭一子百戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced to left regional commander and one son was ennobled as a hundred-household commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left regional commander, and one son received a hereditary hundred-household command.

sentences.zh: 震父棟，前陣亡。

translations.literal: Zhen's father Dong had earlier died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's father Dong had fallen in battle years before.

sentences.zh: 震辭蔭子，乞父祭葬，帝喜而許之。

translations.literal: Zhen declined the ennoblement for his son and begged funeral rites for his father; the emperor was pleased and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen declined the ennoblement for his son and asked instead for proper funeral honors for his father; the emperor gladly agreed.

sentences.zh: 毛伯溫督師，與震修鎮邊諸堡，不數月工成。

translations.literal: Mao Bowen supervised the army; together with Zhen he repaired the border forts, and within a few months the work was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mao Bowen's overall command, Zhen rebuilt the frontier forts, finishing the work within months.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太保，賜其家銀幣，加贈太保，謚武壯。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; silver and silks were bestowed on his family, then he was further posthumously made Grand Tutor, with the posthumous title Martial and Strong.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; the court gave his family silver and silks, then raised him to Grand Tutor with the posthumous name Martial and Strong.

sentences.zh: 震有機略，號令明審。

translations.literal: Zhen had stratagem and resource, and his orders were clear and exact.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was resourceful, and his orders were always clear and firm.

sentences.zh: 前後百十戰，未嘗少挫。

translations.literal: In more than a hundred battles before and after, he never suffered the least setback.
translations.idiomatic: In well over a hundred engagements he never once suffered a real defeat.

sentences.zh: 時率健兒出塞劫敵營，或議其啟釁。

translations.literal: He often led his hardy warriors beyond the border to raid enemy camps, and some argued that he was provoking trouble.
translations.idiomatic: He often led his tough fighters across the border to strike enemy camps, and some accused him of provoking war.

sentences.zh: 震曰：「凡啟釁者，謂寇不擾邊，我橫挑邀功也。

translations.literal: Zhen said: "Those who speak of provoking trouble mean that the raiders are not troubling the border and that I am recklessly picking fights to claim merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen replied: "People call it provocation when the enemy is quiet and we pick a fight for glory.

sentences.zh: 今數深入，乃不思一挫之耶？」

translations.literal: Now they have repeatedly penetrated deep—are we not to think of giving them one defeat?"
translations.idiomatic: But they raid deep into our territory again and again—should we not strike back at least once?

sentences.zh: 震歿，健兒無所歸。

translations.literal: When Zhen died, the hardy warriors had nowhere to go.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen died, his warriors were left without a leader.

sentences.zh: 守臣以聞，編之伍，邊將猶頗得其力。

translations.literal: The defending officials reported it; they were enrolled in companies, and frontier generals still drew considerable strength from them.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials reported the situation, enrolled them in regular units, and frontier commanders still found them highly useful.

sentences.zh: 代震者遼東祝雄，起家世蔭。

translations.literal: Zhen's successor was Zhu Xiong of Liaodong, who rose through hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was succeeded by Zhu Xiong of Liaodong, who entered service through hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 歷都督僉事。

translations.literal: He rose through the post of junior regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually reached junior regional commander.

sentences.zh: 自山西副總兵遷鎮大同。

translations.literal: From vice regional commander in Shanxi he was transferred to command Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He moved from vice regional commander in Shanxi to command Datong.

sentences.zh: 被劾解職，起鎮薊州。

translations.literal: Impeached and dismissed from office, he was later raised to command Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After impeachment and dismissal, he was later recalled to command Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 善撫士，治軍肅。

translations.literal: He was skilled in comforting troops and disciplined in governing the army.
translations.idiomatic: He treated his men well and ran a tight army.

sentences.zh: 寇入塞，率子弟為士卒先。

translations.literal: When raiders entered the border, he led his sons and younger brothers ahead of the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders crossed the border, he put his sons and kinsmen at the head of the charge.

sentences.zh: 子少卻，行法不貸。

translations.literal: If a son fell back even slightly, he enforced the law without mercy.
translations.idiomatic: If a son so much as flinched, he punished him by the full letter of military law.

sentences.zh: 世宗書其名禦屏。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong wrote his name on the imperial screen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong had his name inscribed on the imperial screen of favored officers.

sentences.zh: 為將三十年，布袍氈笠，不異卒伍。

translations.literal: As a general for thirty years he wore cloth robes and felt hats no different from the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years as a commander he dressed in plain cloth and felt hat, indistinguishable from his men.

sentences.zh: 既歿，遺貲僅供殮具。

translations.literal: After his death his estate barely sufficed for burial goods.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his estate barely covered the cost of his coffin.

sentences.zh: 薊人祠祀之。

translations.literal: The people of Jizhou enshrined and sacrificed to him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jizhou raised a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 王效，延綏人。

translations.literal: Wang Xiao was a native of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiao came from Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 讀書能文辭，嫻韜略。

translations.literal: He read books and could compose literary pieces, and was versed in military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He was literate and skilled in prose, and well versed in military strategy.

sentences.zh: 騎射絕人，中武會試。

translations.literal: In horsemanship and archery he surpassed others, and he passed the military metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: An exceptional horseman and archer, he passed the military metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，累官都指揮僉事，充延綏右參將。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign he rose through successive posts to junior regional commander and served as right assistant commander on the Yan-sui front.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiajing he rose to junior regional commander and served as right assistant commander on the Yan-sui front.

sentences.zh: 出神木塞，搗寇雙乃山，斬獲多。

translations.literal: Going out from Shenmu Pass he struck the raiders at Shuangnai Mountain with many killed and captured.
translations.idiomatic: Sallying from Shenmu Pass, he raided the enemy at Shuangnai Mountain and took many heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 尋擢延綏副總兵。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to vice regional commander of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice regional commander on the Yan-sui front.

sentences.zh: 十一年冬，進署都督僉事，充總兵官，代周尚文鎮寧夏。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year he was advanced to acting junior regional commander, appointed regional commander-in-chief, and replaced Zhou Shangwen at Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eleventh year he became acting junior regional commander and regional commander-in-chief at Ningxia, succeeding Zhou Shangwen.

sentences.zh: 吉囊犯鎮遠關，效與梁震敗之柳門。

translations.literal: Jinong invaded Zhenyuan Pass; Xiao and Liang Zhen defeated him at Liumen.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinong attacked Zhenyuan Pass, Xiao and Liang Zhen drove him off at Liumen.

sentences.zh: 追北蜂窩山，蹙溺之河，斬首百四十有奇。

translations.literal: Pursuing north to Fengwo Mountain, they pressed them into the river and drowned them, beheading more than a hundred and forty.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing north to Fengwo Mountain, they drove the enemy into the river and drowned many, taking more than 140 heads.

sentences.zh: 璽書獎賚。

translations.literal: An imperial letter of commendation and rewards were sent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a letter of commendation and rewards.

sentences.zh: 吉囊十萬騎復窺花馬池，效、震拒之不得入，轉犯幹溝。

translations.literal: Jinong with a hundred thousand horsemen again probed Huama Pool; Xiao and Zhen barred him and he could not enter, then turned to invade Gangan Ravine.
translations.idiomatic: Jinong returned with a hundred thousand horsemen to probe Huama Pool; Xiao and Zhen kept him out, so he turned toward Gangan Ravine.

sentences.zh: 震分兵擊，遂趨固原。

translations.literal: Zhen divided his troops to strike, and the enemy then hurried toward Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen split his force to strike, and the enemy veered toward Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 總兵官劉文力戰，寇趨青山峴，大掠安定、會寧。

translations.literal: Regional commander Liu Wen fought fiercely, but the raiders turned toward Qingshan Pass and plundered Anding and Huining on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Liu Wen fought hard, but the raiders swung toward Qingshan Pass and ravaged Anding and Huining.

sentences.zh: 效方敗別部於鼠湖，追至沙湖，疾移師往援，破之安定，再破之靈州，先後斬首百五十余級。

translations.literal: Xiao had just defeated another division at Shuhu Lake and pursued to Shahu; he swiftly shifted his army to the rescue, defeated them at Anding, and defeated them again at Lingzhou, beheading more than a hundred and fifty in all.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao had just routed another enemy band at Shuhu Lake and pursued to Shahu; he wheeled his troops to the rescue, broke the raiders at Anding, and defeated them again at Lingzhou, taking more than 150 heads in all.

sentences.zh: 總制三邊尚書唐龍以大捷聞，而巡按御史奏諸將失事罪。

translations.literal: Minister Tang Long, overall commander of the three frontiers, reported a great victory, while the investigating censor memorialized the generals' offenses for the mishap.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier minister Tang Long reported a great victory, but the investigating censor charged the generals with failures in the campaign.

sentences.zh: 給事中戚賢往勘，奏：「安、會二縣多殺掠，文當罪。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Qi Xian went to investigate and memorialized: "Anding and Huining suffered much killing and plunder; Wen should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Qi Xian investigated and reported: "Anding and Huining suffered heavy slaughter and looting, and Wen should be held accountable.

sentences.zh: 然麾下卒僅八千，倍道蒙險，攖八九萬方張之寇，殊死戰，宜以功贖。

translations.literal: Yet he had only eight thousand troops under him, marched double-time through danger, and grappled with eighty or ninety thousand raiders at the height of their power in a desperate fight—his merit should redeem his fault.
translations.idiomatic: Yet with only eight thousand men he forced a march through peril and met eighty or ninety thousand raiders at full strength in a desperate battle; his merit should offset his fault.

sentences.zh: 震幹溝，效鼠湖、沙湖、安定、靈州之戰，以孤軍八百，當寇萬余，功俱足錄。

translations.literal: At Gangan Ravine, and in the battles of Shuhu, Shahu, Anding, and Lingzhou, Zhen and Xiao with eight hundred isolated troops faced more than ten thousand raiders—their merits all merit recording.
translations.idiomatic: At Gangan Ravine and in the fights at Shuhu, Shahu, Anding, and Lingzhou, Zhen and Xiao each with only eight hundred men faced more than ten thousand raiders—merits fully worthy of record.

sentences.zh: 龍亦善調度。」

translations.literal: Long also dispatched forces well."
translations.idiomatic: Long too had directed the campaign skillfully."

sentences.zh: 詔文奪職，震、效賚銀幣，龍一子入監。

translations.literal: An edict stripped Wen of office, bestowed silver and silks on Zhen and Xiao, and enrolled one of Long's sons in the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The edict stripped Wen of office, rewarded Zhen and Xiao with silver and silks, and enrolled one of Long's sons in the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 是役也功多，執政尼之，故賞薄。

translations.literal: In this campaign merit was great, but those in power obstructed it, and therefore rewards were meager.
translations.idiomatic: The victory deserved far richer rewards, but court factions blocked it, so the honors were thin.

sentences.zh: 御史周鈇以為言，龍、效、震各加一級，效進都督同知。

translations.literal: Censor Zhou Fu spoke on their behalf; Long, Xiao, and Zhen were each advanced one grade, and Xiao was promoted to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: When censor Zhou Fu protested, Long, Xiao, and Zhen each gained a rank, and Xiao was made regional commander.

sentences.zh: 尋以清水營功，進右都督。

translations.literal: Soon, for merit at Qingshui Camp, he was advanced to right regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his service at Qingshui Camp won him promotion to right regional commander.

sentences.zh: 寇以輕騎犯寧夏，效伏兵打鎧口，俟其半入橫擊，敗之，而防河卒復以戰艘邀斬其奔渡者。

translations.literal: The raiders entered Ningxia with light cavalry; Xiao ambushed them at Dakai Pass, waited until half had entered, then struck across and defeated them, while river-defense soldiers in war vessels intercepted and beheaded those fleeing across the ford.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders entered Ningxia with light cavalry; Xiao ambushed them at Dakai Pass, let half cross, then struck and routed them, while river guards in war junks cut down those fleeing the ford.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，進左都督。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, he was advanced to left regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: On news of the victory he was promoted to left regional commander.

sentences.zh: 寇憤，設伏誘敗之，貶右都督。

translations.literal: The raiders in anger set an ambush and lured him into defeat; he was demoted to right regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy laid an ambush and lured him into a defeat; he was demoted to right regional commander.

sentences.zh: 十六年移鎮宣府。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to command Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒，謚武襄。

translations.literal: The next year he died, with the posthumous title Martial and Assisting.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year and was given the posthumous name Martial and Assisting.

sentences.zh: 效言行謹飭，用兵兼謀勇，威名著西陲。

translations.literal: Xiao's conduct was careful and restrained; in employing troops he combined stratagem and courage, and his renown stood on the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao was disciplined in conduct, combined strategy and courage in battle, and his fame dominated the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 與馬永、梁震、周尚文並為名將。

translations.literal: Together with Ma Yong, Liang Zhen, and Zhou Shangwen he ranked among the famed generals.
translations.idiomatic: He ranks with Ma Yong, Liang Zhen, and Zhou Shangwen among the great generals of the age.

sentences.zh: 劉文者，陽和衛人。

translations.literal: Liu Wen was a native of the Yanghe Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wen came from the Yanghe Guard.

sentences.zh: 襲指揮同知。

translations.literal: He inherited the post of vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to the office of vice commander.

sentences.zh: 屢遷署都督僉事，涼州右副總兵。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to acting junior regional commander and right vice regional commander at Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through acting junior regional commander to right vice regional commander at Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年以總兵官鎮陜西。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiajing he was regional commander-in-chief stationed in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Jiajing he became regional commander-in-chief in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 大破洮、岷叛番若籠、板爾諸族，斬首三百六十有奇。

translations.literal: He routed the rebel Tibetans of the Ruolong and Ban'er clans and others in Tao and Min, beheading more than three hundred and sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He crushed the rebel Tibetan clans Ruolong, Ban'er, and others in Tao and Min, taking more than 360 heads.

sentences.zh: 十一年，寇西掠還，將犯寧夏河東，文擊破之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, as raiders returned from plundering in the west and were about to invade east of the river in Ningxia, Wen attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, as raiders returning from a western raid were about to strike east of the Ningxia River, Wen defeated them.

sentences.zh: 積前功，進都督同知。

translations.literal: Accumulating earlier merit, he was advanced to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: His accumulated service won him promotion to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 後落職，起鎮延綏，改甘肅。

translations.literal: Later he lost office, was raised to command Yan-sui, and was transferred to Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Later dismissed, he was recalled to Yan-sui and then transferred to Gansu.

sentences.zh: 卒，亦謚武襄。

translations.literal: He died and likewise received the posthumous title Martial and Assisting.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he too received the posthumous name Martial and Assisting.

sentences.zh: 周尚文，字彥章，西安後衛人。

translations.literal: Zhou Shangwen, styled Yanzhang, was a native of the Xi'an Rear Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shangwen, styled Yanzhang, came from the Xi'an Rear Guard.

sentences.zh: 幼讀書，粗曉大義。

translations.literal: In youth he read books and had a rough grasp of essential principles.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he studied and gained a working knowledge of the classics.

sentences.zh: 多謀略，精騎射。

translations.literal: He was full of stratagem and skilled in horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was resourceful and an expert horseman and archer.

sentences.zh: 年十六，襲指揮同知。

translations.literal: At sixteen he inherited the post of vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he succeeded to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 屢出塞有功，進指揮使。

translations.literal: Repeated campaigns beyond the border brought merit, and he was advanced to commander.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated forays beyond the border won him promotion to commander.

sentences.zh: 寘鑠反，遏黃河渡口，獲叛賊丁廣等，推掌衛事。

translations.literal: When Zhi Di rebelled, he blocked the Yellow River crossing, captured the rebel Ding Guang and others, and was pushed to take charge of guard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince An rebelled, he held the Yellow River crossing, captured rebels including Ding Guang, and was pressed to take charge of the guard.

sentences.zh: 關內回賊四起，倚南山，尚文次第平之。

translations.literal: Hui rebels rose everywhere within the passes, relying on the southern mountains; Shangwen pacified them one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Hui rebels rose throughout the interior, sheltering in the southern hills; Shangwen suppressed them in succession.

sentences.zh: 御史劉天和劾中貴廖堂系詔獄，事連尚文。

translations.literal: Censor Liu Tianhe impeached the favored eunuch Liao Tang, who was imprisoned by imperial order, and the affair implicated Shangwen.
translations.idiomatic: When censor Liu Tianhe impeached the favored eunuch Liao Tang, who was thrown into prison, Shangwen was dragged into the case.

sentences.zh: 拷掠令引天和，終不承，久之始釋。

translations.literal: Under torture he was made to implicate Tianhe, but he never confessed and was released only after a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Under torture he was pressed to implicate Tianhe, but he never confessed and was released only after a long ordeal.

sentences.zh: 已，守備階州。

translations.literal: Later he served as garrison commander at Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as garrison commander at Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 計擒叛番，進署都指揮僉事，充甘肅遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: By stratagem he captured rebel Tibetans and was advanced to acting junior regional commander, appointed mobile corps general of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: By stratagem he captured rebel Tibetans and was made acting junior regional commander and mobile corps general of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年改寧夏參將。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing he was made assistant commander at Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiajing he became assistant commander at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 尋進都指揮同知，為涼州副總兵。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to regional commander and became vice regional commander at Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to regional commander and made vice regional commander at Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 御史按部莊浪，猝遇寇。

translations.literal: A censor was inspecting Zhuanglang when he suddenly encountered raiders.
translations.idiomatic: While a censor was on inspection in Zhuanglang, raiders struck without warning.

sentences.zh: 尚文亟分軍擁御史，而自引麾下射之，寇乃遁。

translations.literal: Shangwen swiftly divided his army to shield the censor, while he himself led his followers to shoot at them, and the raiders then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen quickly detached troops to shield the censor while he led his own men in archery; the raiders fled.

sentences.zh: 嘗追寇出塞，寇來益眾。

translations.literal: Once in pursuing raiders beyond the border, the enemy came in ever greater numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Once, pursuing raiders beyond the border, he found the enemy growing ever stronger.

sentences.zh: 尚文軍半至，麾下皆恐。

translations.literal: Only half of Shangwen's army had arrived, and those under him were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Only half his force had caught up, and his men were terrified.

sentences.zh: 乃從容下馬，解鞍背崖力戰，所殺傷相當。

translations.literal: He then calmly dismounted, removed the saddle, and with his back to the cliff fought fiercely; kills and wounds on both sides were about equal.
translations.idiomatic: He calmly dismounted, stripped his saddle, and with his back to the cliff fought until casualties were roughly even on both sides.

sentences.zh: 部將丁杲來援，寇始退。

translations.literal: Assistant commander Ding Gao came to the rescue, and the raiders then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Assistant Commander Ding Gao arrived, the raiders finally withdrew.

sentences.zh: 尚文被創甚，乃告歸。

translations.literal: Shangwen was badly wounded and then requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Badly wounded, Shangwen asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 尋起故官。

translations.literal: Soon he was raised to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 吉囊數踏冰入。

translations.literal: Jinong several times crossed on the ice to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Jinong repeatedly crossed the frozen river to raid.

sentences.zh: 尚文築墻百二十里，澆以水，冰滑不可上。

translations.literal: Shangwen built a wall a hundred and twenty li long, poured water over it, and the ice was so slippery none could climb it.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen built a 120-li wall and flooded it so the ice was too slick to climb.

sentences.zh: 冰泮則令力士持長竿鐵鉤，鉤殺渡者。

translations.literal: When the ice melted he had strong men hold long poles with iron hooks and hook and kill those crossing.
translations.idiomatic: When the ice broke up he posted strong men with long poles and iron hooks to drag down anyone who tried to ford.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢署都督僉事，充寧夏總兵官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to acting junior regional commander and appointed regional commander-in-chief at Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became acting junior regional commander and regional commander-in-chief at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 王瓊築邊墻，尚文督其役。

translations.literal: Wang Qiong built the border wall, and Shangwen supervised the labor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Qiong built the frontier wall, Shangwen oversaw the work.

sentences.zh: 且浚渠開屯，軍民利之。

translations.literal: He also dredged canals and opened military colonies, to the benefit of soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: He also dredged canals and opened military farms, to the great benefit of troops and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 寇掠西海，過寧夏，巡撫楊誌學議發兵邀。

translations.literal: Raiders plundered the Western Sea and passed through Ningxia; Grand Coordinator Yang Zhixue proposed dispatching troops to intercept them.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders plundered the Western Sea and passed through Ningxia, Grand Coordinator Yang Zhixue urged an ambush.

sentences.zh: 尚文不從，劾解職。

translations.literal: Shangwen did not agree; he was impeached and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen refused; he was impeached and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 久之，起山西副總兵。

translations.literal: After a long while he was raised as vice regional commander in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he was recalled as vice regional commander in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 寇由偏頭關趨岢嵐，尚文轉戰三百里，破之，與子君佐俱傷，賚銀幣。

translations.literal: Raiders from Piantou Pass hurried toward Kelan; Shangwen fought for three hundred li and defeated them; he and his son Junzuo were both wounded, and silver and silks were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders from Piantou Pass drove toward Kelan, Shangwen fought them for three hundred li and broke them; he and his son Junzuo were both wounded and received imperial silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 尋以總兵官鎮延綏。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed regional commander-in-chief to command Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made regional commander-in-chief on the Yan-sui front.

sentences.zh: 寇犯紅山墩，力戰敗之，被賚。

translations.literal: Raiders attacked Hongshan Beacon; he fought fiercely and defeated them, and received imperial rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders struck Hongshan Beacon, he fought them off and was rewarded by the throne.

sentences.zh: 吉囊復大掠清平堡，坐奪俸。

translations.literal: Jinong again raided Qingping Fort on a large scale; for this his salary was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Jinong raided Qingping Fort again, and Shangwen was penalized with loss of salary.

sentences.zh: 尚文優將才，負氣桀傲，所至與文吏競。

translations.literal: Shangwen excelled in military talent, was proud and overbearing, and wherever he went he contended with civil officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen was a gifted commander, proud and headstrong, and everywhere he served he clashed with civil officials.

sentences.zh: 文吏又往往挫折之，以故彌不相得。

translations.literal: Civil officials also often thwarted him, and for this reason they became ever more incompatible.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials in turn often checked him, so the two sides grew ever more hostile.

sentences.zh: 巡撫賈啟劾尚文老誖，兵部請調之甘肅。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Jia Qi impeached Shangwen as senile and perverse; the Ministry of War requested that he be transferred to Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Jia Qi accused Shangwen of senility and obstinacy, and the Ministry of War asked to transfer him to Gansu.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，各奪其俸。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree, and both had their salaries confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, and both men had their salaries stripped.

sentences.zh: 巡按張光祖言兩人必不可共處，乃革尚文任，亦貶啟秩。

translations.literal: Investigating censor Zhang Guangzu said the two could by no means serve together; Shangwen's post was then abolished, and Qi's rank was also reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Zhang Guangzu declared that the two could not serve together; Shangwen was dismissed and Qi's rank was lowered as well.

sentences.zh: 吉囊大入，抵固原。

translations.literal: Jinong invaded on a large scale and reached Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jinong launched a major invasion and pushed as far as Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 天和時已為總督，激尚文立功。

translations.literal: Tianhe was by then already governor-general and urged Shangwen to achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: Tianhe was already governor-general by then and pressed Shangwen to win distinction in battle.

sentences.zh: 奮擊之黑水苑，殺其子號小十王者，獲首功百三十余。

translations.literal: He fought fiercely against them at Heishui Garden, killed Jinong's son styled the Little Ten King, and took more than a hundred and thirty heads for merit.
translations.idiomatic: He drove the enemy hard at Heishui Garden, killed Jinong's son known as the Little Ten King, and claimed more than a hundred and thirty heads.

sentences.zh: 乃以為都督同知。

translations.literal: He was then made regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was promoted to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，用薦為東官廳聽征總兵官兼僉後府事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, on recommendation he was made campaign-attendance regional commander-in-chief at the Dongguan Office and concurrently served in the Rear Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was recommended as campaign-attendance regional commander at the Dongguan Office, with concurrent duties in the Rear Office.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩為禮部尚書，子世蕃官後府都事，驕蹇。

translations.literal: Yan Song was Minister of Rites; his son Shifan held the post of director in the Rear Office and was arrogant and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song was Minister of Rites, and his son Shifan, a director in the Rear Office, was insufferably arrogant.

sentences.zh: 尚文面叱，將劾奏之，嵩謝得免。

translations.literal: Shangwen rebuked him to his face and was about to impeach him; Song apologized and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen publicly berated him and prepared to impeach him; Yan Song apologized and escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 調世蕃治中，以避尚文，銜次骨。

translations.literal: Shifan was transferred to director of affairs to avoid Shangwen, and he bore a grudge to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan was transferred to another post to keep him away from Shangwen, and he nursed a hatred that went to the bone.

sentences.zh: 其秋以總兵官鎮大同，請增餉及馬。

translations.literal: That autumn he was made regional commander-in-chief at Datong and requested increased pay and horses.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he took command at Datong and asked for more funds and horses.

sentences.zh: 兵部言尚文陳請過當，方被詔切責，而尚文與巡撫趙錦不協，乞休，弗允，日相構。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War said Shangwen's petitions were excessive; he had just been sharply rebuked by imperial edict, yet Shangwen and Grand Coordinator Zhao Jin were at odds; he begged to retire, was not permitted, and each day they plotted against each other.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War said Shangwen's requests were excessive, and he had just been sharply rebuked by edict; he and Grand Coordinator Zhao Jin could not work together, and though he asked to retire and was refused, the two feuded daily.

sentences.zh: 御史王三聘乞移之他鎮。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Sanpin asked that he be transferred to another command.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Sanpin urged that Shangwen be moved to another post.

sentences.zh: 廷議：大同敵沖，尚文假此避，不宜墮其奸謀。

translations.literal: Court deliberation held: Datong was the enemy's main thrust; Shangwen was using this as a pretext to avoid duty, and one should not fall into his scheming.
translations.idiomatic: The court decided that Datong bore the brunt of enemy pressure, that Shangwen was using the dispute to shirk duty, and that they must not play into his scheme.

sentences.zh: 乃以錦為甘肅巡撫。

translations.literal: Jin was then made grand coordinator of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jin was instead transferred to Gansu as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 吉囊數萬騎犯前衛。

translations.literal: Jinong with tens of thousands of horsemen attacked the vanguard guard.
translations.idiomatic: Jinong invaded the vanguard guard with tens of thousands of horsemen.

sentences.zh: 尚文與戰黑山，殺其子滿罕歹，追至涼城。

translations.literal: Shangwen fought him at Heishan, killed his son Manhandai, and pursued to Liangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen met him at Heishan, killed his son Manhandai, and chased the enemy to Liangcheng.

sentences.zh: 斬獲多，進右都督。

translations.literal: Many were killed and captured; he was advanced to right regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: With many kills and captures to his credit, he was promoted to right regional commander.

sentences.zh: 已，寇由宣府逼畿甸，出大同塞而北。

translations.literal: Later the raiders from Xuanfu pressed toward the capital region, then passed out through the Datong pass and turned north.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward raiders from Xuanfu threatened the capital approaches, then withdrew north through the Datong frontier.

sentences.zh: 尚文邀之，稍有俘獲。

translations.literal: Shangwen intercepted them and took some captives and booty.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen intercepted them and took a modest haul of prisoners and spoils.

sentences.zh: 後寇復大舉，犯鵓鴿谷，將南下。

translations.literal: Later the raiders again came in force, entered Bobo Valley, and were about to drive south.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders returned in strength, entered Bobo Valley, and prepared to push south.

sentences.zh: 尚文備陽和，遣騎四出邀寇。

translations.literal: Shangwen made ready at Yanghe and sent horsemen out on all sides to intercept the raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen stood ready at Yanghe and sent cavalry out in every direction to intercept them.

sentences.zh: 寇遁，賜敕獎勞之。

translations.literal: The raiders fled, and an imperial edict was bestowed to reward and commend him.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders withdrew, and the throne sent an edict of commendation and reward.

sentences.zh: 總督翁萬達議築邊墻，自宣府西陽和至大同開山口，延袤二百余裏，以屬尚文。

translations.literal: Governor-General Weng Wanda proposed building a border wall from Yanghe west of Xuanfu to Kaishankou at Datong, extending more than two hundred li, and assigning it to Shangwen.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Weng Wanda proposed a border wall from Yanghe west of Xuanfu to Kaishankou at Datong, more than two hundred li long, to be placed under Shangwen's charge.

sentences.zh: 乃益築陽和以西至山西丫角山，凡四百余裏，敵臺千余。

translations.literal: He then further built from west of Yanghe to Yajiao Mountain in Shanxi, altogether more than four hundred li, with over a thousand enemy towers.
translations.idiomatic: He extended the work west from Yanghe to Yajiao Mountain in Shanxi—more than four hundred li in all, with over a thousand watchtowers.

sentences.zh: 斥屯田四萬余頃，益軍萬三千有奇。

translations.literal: More than forty thousand qing of garrison farmland were opened, and the army was increased by a little over thirteen thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: More than forty thousand qing of garrison land were brought under cultivation, and the force was expanded by over thirteen thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其功，進左都督，加太子太保，永除屯稅。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his achievement, advanced him to left regional commander, added the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and permanently exempted garrison taxes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his work, promoted him to left regional commander and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and permanently abolished garrison taxes.

sentences.zh: 叛人充灼召小王子寇邊，尚文偵得其使者，加太保，蔭子錦衣世千戶。

translations.literal: The defector Chong Zhuo summoned the Lesser King to raid the border; Shangwen detected his messenger, was made Grand Preceptor, and his son was granted hereditary thousand-household rank in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the defector Chong Zhuo summoned the Lesser King to raid the frontier, Shangwen intercepted his messenger; he was made Grand Preceptor, and his son received hereditary thousand-household rank in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 終明之世，總兵官加三公者，尚文一人而已。

translations.literal: Throughout the Ming dynasty, of regional commanders-in-chief raised to the Three Dukes, Shangwen alone was such a one.
translations.idiomatic: Through the whole Ming dynasty, Shangwen alone among regional commanders was ever raised to one of the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 初，俺答及吉囊諸子盛強，諸邊歲受其患，大同尤甚。

translations.literal: At first Altan and Jinong and their sons were flourishing and strong; the border regions suffered from them year after year, and Datong especially so.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Altan, Jinong, and their sons had been at the height of their power; the frontiers suffered yearly, and Datong worst of all.

sentences.zh: 自尚文蒞鎮，與總督萬達、巡撫詹榮規畫戰守備邊，民息肩者數年。

translations.literal: From the time Shangwen took command, together with Governor-General Wanda and Grand Coordinator Zhan Rong he planned defense and border preparedness; the people rested their shoulders for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shangwen took command, he and Governor-General Wanda and Grand Coordinator Zhan Rong planned defense together, and the people enjoyed years of relief.

sentences.zh: 尚文益招叛人，孤敵勢，歸者相屬。

translations.literal: Shangwen further recruited defectors, isolated the enemy's strength, and those who returned followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen also recruited defectors, isolating the enemy, and deserters kept coming over in steady streams.

sentences.zh: 二十七年八月，俺答伏兵五堡旁，誘指揮顧相等出，圍之彌陀山。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-seventh year, Altan hid troops beside the Five Forts, lured Commander Gu Xiang and others out, and surrounded them at Mount Mituo.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twenty-seventh year Altan ambushed troops near the Five Forts, drew Commander Gu Xiang and his men out, and trapped them on Mount Mituo.

sentences.zh: 尚文急督副總兵林椿、參將呂勇、遊擊李梅及二子君佐、君仁出塞援，圍始解。

translations.literal: Shangwen urgently directed Vice Regional Commander Lin Chun, Assistant Commander Lü Yong, Mobile Corps General Li Mei, and his two sons Junzuo and Junren to go beyond the border in relief, and only then was the siege lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen hurried Vice Regional Commander Lin Chun, Assistant Commander Lü Yong, Mobile Corps General Li Mei, and his sons Junzuo and Junren across the border to the rescue, and the siege was finally broken.

sentences.zh: 相及指揮周奉，千戶呂愷、郝經等已陣歿。

translations.literal: Xiang, Commander Zhou Feng, thousand-household officers Lü Kai, Hao Jing, and others had already died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xiang, Commander Zhou Feng, and thousand-household officers Lü Kai and Hao Jing were already dead on the field.

sentences.zh: 尚文轉戰，次野口，伏突起。

translations.literal: Shangwen fought on the move; when he halted at Yekou, ambush troops suddenly rose up.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen fought on as he withdrew, but at Yekou an ambush sprang up.

sentences.zh: 殊死戰，斬其長一人。

translations.literal: He fought a desperate battle and beheaded one of their chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: In a desperate fight he cut down one of their leaders.

sentences.zh: 相持月余乃引去。

translations.literal: They faced each other for more than a month before the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The two sides grappled for more than a month before the enemy pulled back.

sentences.zh: 尚文設伏，殺其殿卒而還。

translations.literal: Shangwen set an ambush, killed their rearguard, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen laid an ambush, cut down the enemy rearguard, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 尚文三子俱罪戍，至是以父功得釋。

translations.literal: All three of Shangwen's sons had been sentenced to garrison duty for crimes; now through their father's merit they were released.
translations.idiomatic: All three of Shangwen's sons had been sentenced to frontier service for crimes; now they were freed on account of their father's service.

sentences.zh: 俺答數萬騎犯宣府，萬達檄尚文大破之曹家莊。

translations.literal: Altan with tens of thousands of horsemen invaded Xuanfu; Wanda ordered Shangwen, who routed them at Caojiazhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Altan invaded Xuanfu with tens of thousands of horsemen; Weng Wanda dispatched Shangwen, who shattered them at Caojiazhuang.

sentences.zh: 錄功兼太子太傅，賜賚有加。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was also made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; rewards were bestowed beyond the usual measure.
translations.idiomatic: His victory was recorded and he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent as well, with rewards beyond the usual measure.

sentences.zh: 其年卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same year, at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 尚文清約愛士，得士死力。

translations.literal: Shangwen was frugal and loved his men, and he won soldiers' utmost loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen lived plainly and cared for his men, and they served him unto death.

sentences.zh: 善用間，知敵中曲折，故戰輒有功。

translations.literal: He was skilled in using spies, knew the twists and turns within the enemy camp, and therefore in battle always achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was adept with spies and knew the enemy's inner workings, so his battles usually ended in victory.

sentences.zh: 自二十年後，俺答頻擾邊。

translations.literal: From after the twentieth year, Altan frequently harassed the border.
translations.idiomatic: After the twentieth year Altan raided the frontier again and again.

sentences.zh: 宿將王效、馬永、梁震皆前死，惟尚文存，威名最盛。

translations.literal: Veteran generals Wang Xiao, Ma Yong, and Liang Zhen had all died earlier; only Shangwen remained, and his renown was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: The veteran generals Wang Xiao, Ma Yong, and Liang Zhen were already dead; Shangwen alone remained, and his fame stood highest.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩父子謀傾陷。

translations.literal: Yan Song and his son plotted to bring him down.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song and his son plotted to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 功高，帝方籍以抗強敵，讒不得入。

translations.literal: His achievements were great; the emperor was then relying on him to resist a strong enemy, and slander could not penetrate.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were too great; the emperor still needed him against a formidable foe, and no slander could reach him.

sentences.zh: 暨卒，格恤典不予，給事中沈束以為言。

translations.literal: When he died, posthumous honors and condolence rites were withheld; Supervising Secretary Shen Shu spoke on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the usual posthumous honors were denied; Supervising Secretary Shen Shu protested.

sentences.zh: 嵩激帝怒，錮束詔獄。

translations.literal: Song incited the emperor's anger, and Shu was imprisoned in the edict prison.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song provoked the emperor's wrath, and Shen Shu was thrown into the edict prison.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，始贈太傅，謚武襄。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended the throne, Shangwen was at last posthumously made Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Muzong took the throne was Shangwen posthumously made Grand Tutor with the posthumous name Wuxiang.

sentences.zh: 趙國忠，字伯進，錦州衛人，嗣指揮職。

translations.literal: Zhao Guozhong, styled Bojin, was a native of Jinzhou Guard and succeeded to the post of commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guozhong, styled Bojin, came from Jinzhou Guard and inherited a commander's commission.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年舉武會試，進都指揮僉事，守備叆陽。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiajing he passed the military metropolitan examination, was advanced to junior regional commander, and served as garrison commander at Aiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Jiajing he passed the military metropolitan examination, became junior regional commander, and was posted as garrison commander at Aiyang.

sentences.zh: 擢錦義右參將。

translations.literal: He was promoted to right assistant commander of Jin-Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right assistant commander on the Jin-Yi front.

sentences.zh: 連破敵，增秩，賜金幣，進署都督僉事，為遼東總兵官。

translations.literal: He repeatedly defeated the enemy, received increased rank, was granted gold and silks, was advanced to acting junior regional commander, and became regional commander-in-chief of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated victories he was promoted, rewarded with gold and silks, made acting junior regional commander, and appointed regional commander-in-chief of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 禦敵有功，斬級百七十有奇。

translations.literal: In repelling the enemy he achieved merit and took more than a hundred and seventy heads.
translations.idiomatic: In defending against the enemy he distinguished himself, claiming more than a hundred and seventy heads.

sentences.zh: 進都督同知，賜賚逾等。

translations.literal: He was advanced to regional commander, and rewards were bestowed beyond the usual grade.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regional commander and rewarded beyond the usual measure.

sentences.zh: 敵以八百騎從鴉鶻關入。

translations.literal: The enemy with eight hundred horsemen entered through Yahugu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Eight hundred enemy horsemen came in through Yahugu Pass.

sentences.zh: 都指揮康雲戰歿，裨將三人亦死，詔國忠戴罪立功。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Kang Yun died in battle, three subordinate generals also died, and Guozhong was ordered to redeem his fault by achieving merit.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Kang Yun was killed in battle along with three subordinate generals, and Guozhong was ordered to redeem himself through service.

sentences.zh: 已，坐事被劾，命白衣視事。

translations.literal: Later, for an offense he was impeached and ordered to serve in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was impeached for misconduct and ordered to serve in plain clothes while retaining his duties.

sentences.zh: 守備張文瀚禦敵死，國忠坐解任。

translations.literal: Garrison Commander Zhang Wenhan died repelling the enemy; Guozhong was dismissed from office for this.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison Commander Zhang Wenhan was killed defending against the enemy, and Guozhong was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 尋起西官廳右參將，授都督僉事，提督東官廳。

translations.literal: Soon he was raised as right assistant commander of the Xiguan Office, appointed junior regional commander, and put in charge of the Dongguan Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as right assistant commander of the Xiguan Office, made junior regional commander, and placed in charge of the Dongguan Office.

sentences.zh: 俺答大舉犯宣府，總兵官趙卿不任戰，命國忠代之。

translations.literal: Altan invaded Xuanfu on a large scale; Regional Commander Zhao Qing could not bear the fighting, and Guozhong was ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Altan launched a major invasion of Xuanfu, Regional Commander Zhao Qing proved unequal to the fight, and Guozhong was ordered to replace him.

sentences.zh: 至岔道，寇已為周尚文所敗，東走。

translations.literal: When he reached Chadao, the raiders had already been defeated by Zhou Shangwen and were fleeing east.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Chadao, Zhou Shangwen had already beaten the raiders, who were retreating east.

sentences.zh: 國忠命參將孫勇率精卒逆擊於大滹沱，敗之。

translations.literal: Guozhong ordered Assistant Commander Sun Yong to lead picked troops in a counterattack at the Great Hutuo and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong sent Assistant Commander Sun Yong with elite troops to strike them at the Great Hutuo and routed them.

sentences.zh: 與尚文分道擊，寇盡走，以功受賚。

translations.literal: Together with Shangwen he attacked by separate routes; the raiders all fled, and for his merit he received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He and Shangwen struck by separate routes until the raiders were driven off entirely, and he was rewarded for his service.

sentences.zh: 復坐寇入，降俸二等。

translations.literal: Again, because raiders had entered, his salary was reduced by two grades.
translations.idiomatic: He was again penalized when raiders broke through, and his salary was cut by two grades.

sentences.zh: 俺答薄京師，國忠趨入衛，壁沙河北。

translations.literal: Altan pressed close to the capital; Guozhong hurried to enter in defense and fortified north of the Shahe River.
translations.idiomatic: When Altan threatened the capital, Guozhong rushed to its defense and entrenched north of the Shahe River.

sentences.zh: 已，移護諸陵。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to guard the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: He was later reassigned to guard the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 寇騎至天壽山，見國忠陣紅門前，不敢入。

translations.literal: Enemy horsemen reached Tianshou Mountain, saw Guozhong arrayed before the Red Gate, and did not dare enter.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy cavalry reached Tianshou Mountain, saw Guozhong drawn up before the Red Gate, and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，再鎮遼東。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he again commanded Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he returned to command Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 小王子打來孫以數萬騎寇錦州，國忠禦卻之。

translations.literal: The Lesser King Dalai Sun with tens of thousands of horsemen raided Jinzhou; Guozhong repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser King Dalai Sun invaded Jinzhou with tens of thousands of horsemen, and Guozhong drove him back.

sentences.zh: 明年入獅子口，督參將李廣等逐出塞，斬擒五十人。

translations.literal: The next year they entered Shizikou; he directed Assistant Commander Li Guang and others to drive them beyond the border and killed or captured fifty men.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they came through Shizikou; he sent Assistant Commander Li Guang and others to chase them out and took fifty kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 寇屢入榆林堡、高臺、蛤利河。

translations.literal: Raiders repeatedly entered Yulin Fort, Gaotai, and Hali River.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders struck repeatedly at Yulin Fort, Gaotai, and the Hali River.

sentences.zh: 先後掩擊，獲首功百五十有奇，進秩一等。

translations.literal: In successive ambush attacks he took more than a hundred and fifty heads for merit and was advanced one grade in rank.
translations.idiomatic: In a series of ambushes he claimed more than a hundred and fifty heads and was promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 尋被論罷。

translations.literal: Soon he was criticized and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon impeached and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 國忠善戰，射穿劄，為將有威嚴。

translations.literal: Guozhong was skilled in battle, his arrows pierced targets through and through, and as a general he had dignity and authority.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong was a capable fighter whose arrows pierced armor, and he commanded with real authority.

sentences.zh: 歷兩鎮，繕亭障，練士馬，邊防賴之。

translations.literal: Serving in two commands, he repaired pavilions and barriers, trained soldiers and horses, and the border defense relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Across two frontier commands he repaired defenses, trained troops and horses, and the border depended on him.

sentences.zh: 馬芳，字德馨，蔚州人。

translations.literal: Ma Fang, styled Dexin, was a native of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Fang, styled Dexin, came from Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十歲為北寇所掠，使之牧。

translations.literal: At ten he was captured by northern raiders and made to herd livestock.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he was taken by northern raiders and put to tending herds.

sentences.zh: 芳私以曲木為弓，剡矢射，俺答獵，虎虓其前，芳一發斃之。

translations.literal: Fang secretly made a bow from bent wood, sharpened arrows, and shot; Altan was hunting, a tiger roared before him, and Fang with one shot killed it.
translations.idiomatic: Fang secretly fashioned a bow from bent wood and sharpened arrows; while Altan was hunting, a tiger charged before him, and Fang brought it down with a single shot.

sentences.zh: 乃授以良弓矢、善馬，侍左右。

translations.literal: Altan then gave him fine bow and arrows and a good horse and kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Altan then gave him a fine bow, good arrows, and a strong horse, and kept him in attendance.

sentences.zh: 芳陽為之用，而潛自間道亡歸。

translations.literal: Fang outwardly served him, but secretly by a hidden path fled and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Fang pretended to serve willingly, but slipped away by a hidden route and made his escape home.

sentences.zh: 周尚文鎮大同，奇之，署為隊長。

translations.literal: Zhou Shangwen commanded Datong, marveled at him, and appointed him squad leader.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Shangwen took command at Datong, he was impressed and made Fang a squad leader.

sentences.zh: 數禦寇有功，當得官，以父貧，悉受賞以養。

translations.literal: He repeatedly repelled raiders with merit and ought to have received office, but because his father was poor he took all rewards to support him.
translations.idiomatic: He fought raiders with repeated success and could have won office, but his father was poor, so he took every reward to support him.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十九年秋，寇犯懷柔、順義。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twenty-ninth year of Jiajing, raiders invaded Huairou and Shunyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Jiajing 29 raiders struck Huairou and Shunyi.

sentences.zh: 芳馳斬其將，授陽和衛總旗。

translations.literal: Fang galloped forth and beheaded their general, and was appointed chief pennant of Yanghe Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Fang rode out and cut down an enemy general, and was made chief pennant of Yanghe Guard.

sentences.zh: 寇嘗入威遠，伏驍騎鹽場，而以二十騎挑戰。

translations.literal: Raiders once entered Weiyuan, hid fierce horsemen at the salt flats, and with twenty horsemen offered battle.
translations.idiomatic: Once when raiders entered Weiyuan, they hid elite cavalry at the salt flats and sent twenty horsemen forward to provoke a fight.

sentences.zh: 芳知其詐，用百騎薄伏所，三分其軍銳，以次擊之。

translations.literal: Fang knew it was a ruse; with a hundred horsemen he pressed close to the ambush site, divided his best troops into three parts, and struck them in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Fang saw the trap; he closed on the ambush with a hundred horsemen, split his best troops three ways, and hit them in turn.

sentences.zh: 奮勇跳蕩，敵騎辟易十里，斬首凡九十級。

translations.literal: Fighting boldly and charging about, enemy horsemen gave way for ten li; altogether ninety heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: He fought with fierce charges, and enemy cavalry scattered for ten li; he took ninety heads in all.

sentences.zh: 已，復禦之新平。

translations.literal: Later he again repelled them at Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: He later fought them off again at Xinping.

sentences.zh: 寇營野馬川，克日戰。

translations.literal: The raiders encamped at Yemachuan and set a day for battle.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders camped at Yemachuan and fixed a day for battle.

sentences.zh: 芳度寇且遁，急乘之，斬級益多。

translations.literal: Fang judged that the raiders were about to flee, pressed the pursuit urgently, and took ever more heads.
translations.idiomatic: Fang guessed they would run, pressed the pursuit hard, and took still more heads.
