sentences.zh: 眾方賀，芳遽策馬曰：「賊至矣。」

translations.literal: The troops were just celebrating when Fang suddenly spurred his horse and said, "The bandits have arrived."
translations.idiomatic: The men were still cheering victory when Fang suddenly wheeled his horse and cried, "The enemy is upon us!"

sentences.zh: 趣守險，而身斷後。

translations.literal: He urged them to hold difficult terrain, while he himself covered the rear.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a retreat to defensible ground and took the rear guard himself.

sentences.zh: 頃之，寇果麕至。

translations.literal: Before long, the raiders indeed came in a herd.
translations.idiomatic: In no time the raiders came swarming after them, just as he had said.

sentences.zh: 芳戰益力，寇乃去。

translations.literal: Fang fought with increasing force, and the raiders then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Fang fought all the harder, and the raiders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 亡何，戰泥河，復大破之。

translations.literal: Before long, he fought at Nihe and again routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he fought at Nihe and routed them again.

sentences.zh: 累遷指揮僉事。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Assistant Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Assistant Commander.

sentences.zh: 以功，進都指揮僉事，充宣府遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to Assistant Regional Commander and appointed Mobile Corps General of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: For his exploits he was made Assistant Regional Commander and Mobile Corps General at Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 復以功，超遷都督僉事，隸總督為參將。

translations.literal: Again for merit he was promoted by special advancement to Assistant Regional Commissioner, attached to the Supreme Commander as a Deputy General.
translations.idiomatic: Further exploits won him a special jump promotion to Assistant Regional Commissioner, serving the supreme commander as deputy general.

sentences.zh: 戰鎮山墩不利，奪俸。

translations.literal: At Zhenshandun the battle went badly, and his salary was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: A defeat at Zhenshandun cost him his stipend.

sentences.zh: 已，襲寇有功，進二秩，為右都督。

translations.literal: Later, in a raid on raiders he had merit, was promoted two ranks, and became Right Regional Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Later he struck raiders with success, advanced two ranks, and became Right Regional Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋以功進左，賜蟒袍。

translations.literal: Soon for merit he was advanced to the Left and granted a python robe.
translations.idiomatic: Before long merit earned him promotion to Left Commissioner and the gift of a python robe.

sentences.zh: 偏裨加左都督，自芳始也。

translations.literal: A subordinate general receiving Left Regional Commissioner—this began with Fang.
translations.idiomatic: From Fang onward, subordinate commanders could rise to Left Regional Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，遷薊鎮副總兵，分守建昌。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he was transferred to Deputy Supreme Commander of Jizhen, with separate defense of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-six he became deputy supreme commander at Jizhen, with independent charge of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 土蠻十萬騎薄界嶺口，芳與總兵官歐陽安斬首數十，獲驍騎猛克兔等六人。

translations.literal: Tumen with a hundred thousand horsemen pressed close to Jieling Pass; Fang together with Regional Commander Ouyang An took dozens of heads and captured six men including the fierce horseman Mengketu.
translations.idiomatic: When Tumen brought a hundred thousand horsemen up to Jieling Pass, Fang and Regional Commander Ouyang An took dozens of heads and captured six elite riders, Mengketu among them.

sentences.zh: 寇不知芳在，芳免胄示之，驚曰：「馬太師也！」

translations.literal: The raiders did not know Fang was present; Fang removed his helmet to show himself, and they cried in alarm, "It is Marshal Ma!"
translations.idiomatic: The raiders had not known Fang was there. He lifted his helmet to show his face, and they cried in alarm, "Marshal Ma!"

sentences.zh: 遂卻。

translations.literal: Then they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At that they fell back.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，蔭世總旗。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, his son was granted hereditary chief pennant.
translations.idiomatic: Word of victory earned his son a hereditary chief pennant.

sentences.zh: 未幾，辛愛、把都兒大入，躪遵化、玉田。

translations.literal: Before long Xin Ai and Batuer made a major incursion, trampling Zunhua and Yutian.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xin Ai and Batuer stormed deep into the frontier, ravaging Zunhua and Yutian.

sentences.zh: 芳追戰金山寺有功，而州縣破殘多，總督王忬以下俱獲罪，芳亦貶都督僉事。

translations.literal: Fang pursued and fought at Jinshan Temple with merit, but many prefectures and counties were broken and ruined; Governor Wang Xuan and those below were all punished, and Fang was demoted to Assistant Regional Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Fang fought well in pursuit at Jinshan Temple, but widespread ruin in the prefectures and counties brought punishment on Governor Wang Xuan and his subordinates; Fang was demoted to Assistant Regional Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋移守宣府。

translations.literal: Soon he was shifted to guard Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reassigned to defend Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 寇大入山西，芳一日夜馳五百里及之，七戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Raiders made a major incursion into Shanxi; Fang in one day and night galloped five hundred li and caught them, winning victory in seven battles.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders plunged deep into Shanxi, Fang rode five hundred li in a day and a night to overtake them and won seven battles in a row.

sentences.zh: 已，復為左都督，就擢總兵官，以功進二秩。

translations.literal: Later he was restored as Left Regional Commissioner, was then promoted to Regional Commander, and for merit advanced two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored to Left Commissioner, promoted on the spot to regional commander, and advanced two ranks for merit.

sentences.zh: 寇薄通州，芳入衛，令專護京師。

translations.literal: Raiders pressed close to Tongzhou; Fang entered to defend the capital and was ordered exclusively to protect the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders neared Tongzhou, Fang rushed in to defend the capital and was charged solely with guarding Beijing.

sentences.zh: 寇退，再進一秩。

translations.literal: When the raiders withdrew, he was again promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: After the raiders withdrew, he won another rank.

sentences.zh: 尋與故總兵劉漢出北沙灘，搗寇巢。

translations.literal: Soon together with the former Regional Commander Liu Han he went out to North Shatan and destroyed raider lairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he and the former regional commander Liu Han marched to North Shatan and struck the raiders in their camps.

sentences.zh: 已，坐寇入，令戴罪。

translations.literal: Later, because raiders entered, he was ordered to serve while bearing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when raiders broke through again, he was ordered to redeem himself in battle.

sentences.zh: 四十五年七月，辛愛以十萬騎入西路，芳迎之馬蓮堡。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the forty-fifth year Xin Ai with a hundred thousand horsemen entered by the western route; Fang met him at Malian Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year forty-five Xin Ai brought a hundred thousand horsemen in by the western route, and Fang met him at Malian Fort.

sentences.zh: 堡圮，眾請塞之，不可。

translations.literal: The fort wall had collapsed; the troops asked to block it up, but he would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: The fort walls had crumbled. His men asked to block the breach, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 請登臺，亦不可。

translations.literal: They asked to mount the watchtower; again he would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: They asked to man the watchtower; again he refused.

sentences.zh: 開堡四門，偃旗鼓，寂若無人。

translations.literal: He opened the fort's four gates, lowered flags and drums, and it was silent as if no one were there.
translations.idiomatic: He opened all four gates, furled flags and stilled drums, until the fort seemed deserted.

sentences.zh: 比暮，野燒燭天，囂呼達旦。

translations.literal: By evening, prairie fires lit the sky; shouting and clamor lasted until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: By nightfall fires blazed across the steppe and the enemy shouted and jeered until dawn.

sentences.zh: 芳臥，日中不起，敵騎窺者相屬，莫測所為。

translations.literal: Fang lay abed and did not rise until midday; enemy horsemen who came to spy followed one after another, unable to fathom what he was doing.
translations.idiomatic: Fang slept on and did not rise until noon, while enemy scouts came and went in succession, utterly baffled.

sentences.zh: 明日，芳蹶然起，乘城，指示眾曰：「彼軍多反顧，且走。」

translations.literal: The next day Fang suddenly rose, mounted the wall, pointed to the troops and said, "Their army looks back often—they are about to flee."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Fang leapt up, climbed the wall, and told his men, "They keep glancing back—they are on the verge of running."

sentences.zh: 勒兵追擊，大破之。

translations.literal: He marshaled troops in pursuit and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: He led his men in pursuit and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，或為辛愛謀，以五萬騎犯蔚州，誘芳出，而以五萬騎襲宣府城，可得誌。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, someone plotted for Xin Ai: with fifty thousand horsemen strike Yu Prefecture to lure Fang out, then with fifty thousand horsemen surprise Xuanfu city and they could succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longqing someone plotted for Xin Ai: fifty thousand horsemen would hit Yu Prefecture to draw Fang out, while another fifty thousand would strike Xuanfu itself—the plan could succeed.

sentences.zh: 芳豫伐木環城，寇至不可上，遂解去。

translations.literal: Fang beforehand felled trees to ring the city; when raiders arrived they could not climb up, and then dispersed and left.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had timber felled and stacked around the walls; when the raiders came they could not scale the defenses and broke off the siege.

sentences.zh: 頃之，率參將劉潭等出獨石塞外二百里，襲其帳於長水海。

translations.literal: Before long, leading Deputy General Liu Tan and others he went out beyond Dushi Pass two hundred li and raided their camp at Changshuihai.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he led Deputy General Liu Tan and others two hundred li beyond Dushi Pass and struck their camp at Changshuihai.

sentences.zh: 還至塞，追者及鞍子山。

translations.literal: Returning to the pass, pursuers caught up at Anzishan.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march pursuers caught up at Anzi Mountain.

sentences.zh: 迎戰，又大敗之。

translations.literal: He met them in battle and again routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to fight and routed them again.

sentences.zh: 蔭子千戶。

translations.literal: His son was granted hereditary company commander.
translations.idiomatic: His son received a hereditary company command.

sentences.zh: 芳有膽智，諳敵情，所至先士卒。

translations.literal: Fang had courage and wisdom, understood enemy conditions, and wherever he went he went ahead of the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was brave and shrewd, knew the enemy well, and always led from the front.

sentences.zh: 一歲數出師搗巢，或躬督戰，或遣裨將。

translations.literal: In one year he several times led troops out to destroy lairs, sometimes personally supervising battle, sometimes sending subordinate generals.
translations.idiomatic: In a single year he often marched out to smash enemy camps, sometimes commanding in person, sometimes delegating to his deputies.

sentences.zh: 家蓄健兒，得其死力。

translations.literal: At home he kept stalwart youths and obtained their death-dealing strength.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a household guard of stalwart fighters who would die for him.

sentences.zh: 嘗命三十人出塞四百里，多所斬獲，寇大震。

translations.literal: Once he ordered thirty men to go out beyond the border four hundred li, took many heads and captures, and the raiders were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Once he sent thirty men four hundred li beyond the border; they took many heads and spoils, and the raiders were badly shaken.

sentences.zh: 芳乃帥師至大松林，頓舊興和衛，登高四望，耀兵而還。

translations.literal: Fang then led troops to Great Pine Forest, encamped at old Xinghe Guard, climbed high and looked in the four directions, displayed his forces, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Fang then marched to Great Pine Forest, camped at the old site of Xinghe Guard, climbed a height to survey all around, showed his strength, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時大同被寇，視宣府尤甚。

translations.literal: At that time Datong was ravaged by raiders, even more severely than Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Datong was under heavy raid pressure then, worse even than Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 總督陳其學恐擾畿輔，令總兵官趙岢扼紫荊關。

translations.literal: Supreme Commander Chen Qixue feared disturbance of the capital region and ordered Regional Commander Zhao Ke to hold Zijing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme Commander Chen Qixue, fearing raids on the capital approaches, ordered Regional Commander Zhao Ke to hold Zijing Pass.

sentences.zh: 寇乃縱掠懷仁、山陰間，岢坐貶三秩，遂調芳與易鎮。

translations.literal: Raiders then spread out looting between Huairen and Shanyin; Zhao Ke was punished with demotion of three ranks, and Fang was transferred to swap commands.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders swept through Huairen and Shanyin instead; Zhao Ke was demoted three ranks, and Fang was shifted to swap frontier commands with him.

sentences.zh: 俺答轉犯威遠幾破，會其學率胡鎮等救，而芳軍亦至，相拒十余日，乃走。

translations.literal: Altan turned to attack Weiyuan and nearly broke through; just then Qixue led Hu Zhen and others to the rescue, and Fang's army also arrived; they confronted each other for more than ten days, and then the raiders fled.
translations.idiomatic: Altan turned on Weiyuan and nearly took it; Chen Qixue brought Hu Zhen and others to its relief, Fang's force arrived as well, and after more than ten days of stalemate the raiders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 芳謂諸將曰：「大同非宣府比，與我間一墻耳。

translations.literal: Fang told the generals, "Datong is not to be compared with Xuanfu—it is separated from me by only one wall.
translations.idiomatic: Fang told his officers, "Datong is not like Xuanfu—we are only a wall apart.

sentences.zh: 寇不時至，非大創之不可。」

translations.literal: Raiders come at any time; unless they suffer a heavy blow it will not do."
translations.idiomatic: The raiders strike whenever they please; nothing less than a crushing blow will stop them."

sentences.zh: 乃將兵出右衛，戰威寧海子，破之。

translations.literal: He then led troops out from Right Guard, fought at Weininghaizi, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He marched out from Right Guard, fought at Weininghaizi, and broke them.

sentences.zh: 其年，俺答就撫，塞上遂無事。

translations.literal: That year Altan accepted pacification, and the border was then without incident.
translations.idiomatic: That year Altan submitted to peace terms, and the frontier at last grew quiet.

sentences.zh: 萬歷元年，閱視侍郎吳百朋發芳行賄事，勒閑住。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli, touring Censor Wu Baipeng exposed Fang's bribery affair and ordered him to retire in idleness.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 1 Touring Censor Wu Baipeng exposed Fang's bribery and had him sent home in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 已，起僉書前軍都督府。

translations.literal: Later he was recalled to serve as Registrar of the Forward Army Regional Command.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled as registrar of the Forward Army Command.

sentences.zh: 順義王要賞，聲言渝盟，復用芳鎮宣府。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shunyi demanded rewards and declared the alliance broken; Fang was again employed to command Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Shunyi demanded tribute and threatened to break the treaty, Fang was restored to command at Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 七年以疾乞歸。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, on grounds of illness he requested to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 又二年卒。

translations.literal: Two years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died.

sentences.zh: 芳起行伍，十余年為大帥。

translations.literal: Fang rose from the ranks; in little more than ten years he became a supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had risen from the ranks to supreme command in little more than a decade.

sentences.zh: 戰膳房堡、朔州、登鷹巢、鴿子堂、龍門、萬全右衛、東嶺、孤山、土木、乾莊、岔道、張家堡、得勝堡、大沙灘，大小百十接，身被數十創，以少擊眾，未嘗不大捷。

translations.literal: He fought at Shanfang Fort, Shuozhou, Dengyingchao, Gezitang, Longmen, Wanquan Right Guard, Dongling, Gushan, Tumu, Ganzhuang, Chadadao, Zhangjiapu, Deshengbao, Dashatan—in more than a hundred engagements large and small; he received dozens of wounds on his body; striking the many with the few, he never failed to win a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Shanfang Fort, Shuozhou, Eagle Nest Heights, Pigeon Hall, Longmen, Wanquan Right Guard, East Ridge, Lone Mountain, Tumu, Ganzhuang, Chadadao, Zhangjiapu, Desheng Fort, Great Sandy Beach—well over a hundred battles in all. He took dozens of wounds, yet fighting outnumbered he always won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 擒部長數十人，斬馘無算，威名震邊陲，為一時將帥冠。

translations.literal: He captured dozens of tribal chiefs; heads taken were beyond counting; his fierce name shook the border regions, and he was the crown of generals and commanders of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He took dozens of tribal chiefs captive and heads beyond count; his name shook the frontier, and among the commanders of his day he stood foremost.

sentences.zh: 石州城陷，副將田世威、參將劉寶論死，芳乞寢己蔭子，贖二將罪，為御史所劾，敕戒諭。

translations.literal: When Shizhou city fell, Deputy General Tian Shiwei and Deputy General Liu Bao were sentenced to death; Fang begged to set aside his own hereditary grant for his son to redeem the two generals' guilt, was impeached by a censor, and received an edict of admonition.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizhou fell, Deputy General Tian Shiwei and Deputy General Liu Bao were condemned to death. Fang asked to give up his son's hereditary privilege to spare them; a censor impeached him, and the throne sent a reprimand.

sentences.zh: 後世威復為將，遇芳薄，芳不與校，識者多之。

translations.literal: Later Shiwei again became a general; meeting Fang he treated him coldly, but Fang did not contend with him; the discerning praised this of Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Shiwei later returned to command; he treated Fang coldly when they met, but Fang did not take offense, and thoughtful men admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 二子，棟、林。

translations.literal: He had two sons, Dong and Lin.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Dong and Lin.

sentences.zh: 棟官至都督，無所見。

translations.literal: Dong rose to Regional Commissioner, with nothing noteworthy recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Dong rose to regional commissioner but left no mark in the records.

sentences.zh: 林，由父蔭累官大同參將。

translations.literal: Lin, through his father's privilege, accumulated offices to Deputy General of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Lin inherited his father's privilege and rose to deputy general at Datong.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十年，順義王撦力克縶獻史、車二部長，林以制敵功，進副總兵。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Wanli the Prince of Shunyi Chelik bound and presented two chiefs of the Shi and Che tribes; Lin for merit in controlling the enemy was promoted to Deputy Supreme Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 20 the Prince of Shunyi Chelik bound and delivered two chiefs of the Shi and Che tribes; Lin was promoted to deputy supreme commander for helping check the enemy.

sentences.zh: 二十七年擢署都督僉事，為遼東總兵官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was selected and appointed Acting Assistant Regional Commissioner and became Regional Commander of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-seven he was acting assistant regional commissioner and regional commander of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 林雅好文學，能詩，工書，交遊多名士，時譽籍甚，自許亦甚高。

translations.literal: Lin elegantly loved literature, could compose poetry, was skilled in calligraphy, associated with many eminent scholars; his contemporary reputation was very great, and his self-estimation was also very high.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was a literary man who wrote poetry and practiced calligraphy, kept company with leading scholars, enjoyed wide renown, and thought highly of himself.

sentences.zh: 嘗陳邊務十策，語多觸文吏，寢不行。

translations.literal: Once he submitted ten policies on border affairs; his words often offended civil officials, and they were shelved and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted ten proposals on frontier affairs; much of it affronted the civil bureaucracy, and the plans were buried.

sentences.zh: 稅使高淮橫恣，林力與抗。

translations.literal: Tax commissioner Gao Huai was domineering and unrestrained; Lin vigorously resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Tax commissioner Gao Huai ran rampant; Lin fought him hard.

sentences.zh: 淮劾奏之，坐奪職。

translations.literal: Huai memorialized impeaching him; Lin was punished by loss of office.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huai denounced him at court, and Lin lost his post.

sentences.zh: 給事中侯先春論救，改林戍煙瘴，先春亦左遷二官。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Hou Xianchun argued in his defense; Lin was changed to exile in malarial lands, and Xianchun was also demoted two ranks to the left.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Hou Xianchun pleaded for him; Lin was sent to serve exile in the malarial south, and Hou was demoted two ranks as well.

sentences.zh: 久之，遇赦免。

translations.literal: After a long time he met an amnesty and was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was pardoned by imperial amnesty.

sentences.zh: 遼左用兵，詔林以故官從征。

translations.literal: When Liaodong campaigned militarily, Lin was ordered to follow the expedition with his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out in Liaodong he was recalled to serve at his old rank.

sentences.zh: 楊鎬之四路出師也，令林將一軍由開原出三岔口，而以遊擊竇永澄監北關軍並進。

translations.literal: When Yang Hao sent four routes out on campaign, Lin was ordered to command one army out from Kaiyuan through Sanchakou, while Mobile Corps Commander Dou Yongcheng supervised the Beiguan army advancing together.
translations.idiomatic: In Yang Hao's four-pronged campaign Lin led one corps from Kaiyuan through Sanchakou while Mobile Corps Commander Dou Yongcheng brought the Beiguan force up alongside.

sentences.zh: 林軍至尚間崖結營浚壕，嚴斥堠自衛。

translations.literal: Lin's army reached Shangjianya, encamped, dug trenches, and strictly manned outposts for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Lin camped at Shangjian Cliff, dug trenches, and posted pickets in tight defense.

sentences.zh: 及聞杜松軍敗，方移營，而大清兵已逼。

translations.literal: When he heard that Du Song's army had been defeated, he was just moving camp when the Great Qing army was already pressing close.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Du Song's force had been destroyed, he was still shifting camp when the Qing army was already upon him.

sentences.zh: 乃還兵，別立營，浚壕三周，列火器壕外，更布騎兵於火器外，他士卒皆下馬，結方陣壕內。

translations.literal: He then drew back his troops, established a separate camp, dug three circuits of trenches, arrayed firearms outside the trenches, further deployed cavalry outside the firearms; the other soldiers all dismounted and formed a square formation inside the trenches.
translations.idiomatic: He pulled his men back, pitched a fresh camp, dug three rings of trenches, placed firearms beyond the inner ditch, cavalry beyond the guns, and had the rest dismount and form square inside the works.

sentences.zh: 又一軍西營飛芬山。

translations.literal: Another army encamped to the west at Feifenshan.
translations.idiomatic: A second detachment encamped west at Feifen Mountain.

sentences.zh: 杜松軍既覆，大清兵乘銳薄林軍。

translations.literal: After Du Song's army had been destroyed, the Great Qing army, riding their sharp momentum, pressed close to Lin's army.
translations.idiomatic: With Du Song destroyed, the Qing army swept on at full momentum against Lin.

sentences.zh: 見林壕內軍已與壕外合而陳，縱精騎直前沖之。

translations.literal: Seeing that Lin's troops inside the trenches had already joined with those outside and formed battle lines, they unleashed elite cavalry to charge straight forward.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Lin's inner and outer formations already united in line, they sent elite cavalry in a headlong charge.

sentences.zh: 林軍不能支，遂大敗。

translations.literal: Lin's army could not sustain it and was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's force could not hold and was routed.

sentences.zh: 副將麻巖戰死，林僅以數騎免。

translations.literal: Deputy General Ma Yan died in battle; Lin escaped only with a few horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy General Ma Yan was killed; Lin escaped with only a handful of riders.

sentences.zh: 死者彌山谷，血流尚間崖下，水為之赤。

translations.literal: The dead filled valley and hill; blood flowed below Shangjianya, and the water turned red because of it.
translations.idiomatic: Dead filled the valleys; blood ran below Shangjian Cliff until the stream ran red.

sentences.zh: 大清遂移兵擊飛芬山。

translations.literal: The Great Qing then shifted troops to strike Feifenshan.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing army then turned on Feifen Mountain.

sentences.zh: 僉事潘宗顏等一軍亦覆。

translations.literal: Commissioner Pan Zongyan's army was also destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Pan Zongyan's corps was wiped out as well.

sentences.zh: 北關兵聞之，遂不敢進。

translations.literal: The Beiguan troops upon hearing this dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Beiguan force, hearing this, dared not push forward.

sentences.zh: 林既喪師，謫充為事官，俾守開原。

translations.literal: Lin having lost his army was demoted to probationary officer and ordered to guard Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After losing his army Lin was reduced to probationary status and ordered to hold Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 時蒙古宰賽、煖兔許助林兵，林與結約，恃此不設備。

translations.literal: At that time the Mongols Zaisai and Nuantu promised to aid Lin's troops; Lin made a pact with them and relied on this to make no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol leaders Zaisai and Nuantu had pledged to help; Lin trusted their pact and left his defenses slack.

sentences.zh: 其年六月，大清兵忽臨城。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year the Great Qing army suddenly arrived at the city.
translations.idiomatic: That June the Qing army appeared suddenly before the city.

sentences.zh: 林列眾城外，分少兵登陴。

translations.literal: Lin arrayed his multitude outside the city and sent a few troops to mount the battlements.
translations.idiomatic: Lin drew up his main force outside the walls and kept only a handful of men on the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 大清兵設盾梯進攻，而別以精騎擊破林軍之營東門外者。

translations.literal: The Great Qing army set up shields and ladders to press the attack, while separately using elite cavalry to strike and break those of Lin's army encamped outside the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing brought up shields and scaling ladders while elite cavalry broke the camp Lin had outside the east gate.

sentences.zh: 軍士爭門入，遂乘勢奪門，攻城兵亦逾城入。

translations.literal: Soldiers scrambled to enter the gate; then they seized the momentum and seized the gate, and assault troops also crossed the wall and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers fought to get through the gate; the Qing seized it in the scramble, and assault troops scaled the walls as well.

sentences.zh: 林城外軍望見盡奔。

translations.literal: Lin's army outside the city, seeing this, all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's troops outside the walls broke and ran at the sight.

sentences.zh: 大清兵據城邀擊，壕不得渡，悉殲之。

translations.literal: The Great Qing army held the city and intercepted them in attack; unable to cross the moat, all were annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing held the walls and struck them at the moat; unable to cross, they were slaughtered to the last man.

sentences.zh: 林及副將於化龍、參將高貞、遊擊於守誌、守備何懋官等，皆死焉。

translations.literal: Lin together with Deputy General Yu Hualong, Deputy General Gao Zhen, Mobile Corps Commander Yu Shouzhi, Garrison Commander He Maoguan, and others all died there.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, Deputy General Yu Hualong, Deputy General Gao Zhen, Mobile Corps Commander Yu Shouzhi, Garrison Commander He Maoguan, and others all died in the fall.

sentences.zh: 尋贈都督同知，進世蔭二秩。

translations.literal: Soon he was posthumously granted Associate Regional Commissioner and his hereditary privilege was advanced two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posthumously made Associate Regional Commissioner and his family's hereditary rank was raised two steps.

sentences.zh: 林雖更歷邊鎮，然未經強敵，無大將才。

translations.literal: Although Lin had served in turn at border commands, he had never faced strong enemies and lacked the talent of a great general.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had held border commands, but he had never met a truly formidable foe and lacked a great commander's gifts.

sentences.zh: 當事以虛名用之，故敗。

translations.literal: Those in power employed him for an empty reputation, and therefore he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Court appointees used him for his renown alone, and that was why he failed.

sentences.zh: 林五子，燃、熠、炯、爌，飈。

translations.literal: Lin had five sons: Ran, Yi, Jiong, Huang, and Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had five sons—Ran, Yi, Jiong, Huang, and Biao.

sentences.zh: 燃、熠，戰死尚間崖。

translations.literal: Ran and Yi died in battle at Shangjianya.
translations.idiomatic: Ran and Yi were killed in battle at Shangjian Cliff.

sentences.zh: 炯，天啟中湖廣總兵官。

translations.literal: Jiong, during the Tianqi reign, was regional commander of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong served as regional commander of Huguang during the Tianqi reign.

sentences.zh: 協討貴州叛賊，從王三善至大方，數戰皆捷。

translations.literal: He assisted in campaigning against rebel bandits in Guizhou, followed Wang Sanshan to Dafang, and was victorious in battle after battle.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Guizhou rebels, marching with Wang Sanshan to Dafang and winning victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 已，大敗，三善自殺。

translations.literal: Before long they suffered a great defeat, and Sanshan killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward they were routed in a major defeat, and Sanshan took his own life.

sentences.zh: 炯潰歸。

translations.literal: Jiong fled in rout and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong broke and fled home.

sentences.zh: 得疾而卒。

translations.literal: He contracted illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 爌幼習兵略，天啟中為遼東遊擊。

translations.literal: Huang studied military strategy from youth; during Tianqi he served as mobile corps commander in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Huang had studied military strategy since boyhood and, during the Tianqi reign, served as a mobile corps commander in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 督師閣部孫承宗以其父死王事，獎用之，命代王楹守中右所。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary and supreme commander Sun Chengzong, because his father had died in the state's service, rewarded and employed him, ordering him to replace Wang Ying in guarding the Central-Right Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary and supreme commander Sun Chengzong, honoring him because his father had died in the state's service, gave him preferment and ordered him to replace Wang Ying in holding the Central-Right Garrison.

sentences.zh: 及巡撫袁崇煥更營制，以故官掌前鋒左營。

translations.literal: When Grand Coordinator Yuan Chonghuan reorganized the camp system, Huang retained his former rank and commanded the Vanguard Left Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Coordinator Yuan Chonghuan reorganized the camp structure, Huang kept his old rank and took command of the Vanguard Left Battalion.

sentences.zh: 數有功，屢遷至副總兵，守徐州。

translations.literal: He achieved merit repeatedly and was promoted again and again until he became deputy regional commander, guarding Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated victories he rose through the ranks to deputy regional commander and was posted to guard Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎八年正月，賊陷鳳陽，大掠而去。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year of Chongzhen, bandits captured Fengyang, plundered on a great scale, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year of the Chongzhen reign, rebels seized Fengyang, looted the city thoroughly, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 爌及守備駱舉率兵入，以恢復告，遂留戍其地。

translations.literal: Huang and garrison commander Luo Ju led troops in, reported the recovery, and then remained to garrison the place.
translations.idiomatic: Huang and garrison commander Luo Ju marched in, reported the city's recovery, and were left to garrison the area.

sentences.zh: 八月，賊擾河南。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, bandits harassed Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month rebels raided Henan.

sentences.zh: 總督朱大典命移駐潁、毫。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Zhu Dadian ordered him to redeploy and encamp at Ying and Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhu Dadian ordered him to shift his camp to the Ying and Bo region.

sentences.zh: 事定，還徐州。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, he returned to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once the crisis had passed, he returned to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，賊犯桐城，爌赴救，破之羅唱河。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, bandits invaded Tongcheng; Huang rushed to the rescue and defeated them at the Luochang River.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when rebels struck Tongcheng, Huang hurried to its relief and routed them on the Luochang River.

sentences.zh: 尋以護陵功，增秩一級。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, for his merit in guarding the imperial tombs, his rank was raised one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, his rank was raised one grade for his service in protecting the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 歸德、徐州間有地曰朱家廠，土寇據之，時出掠。

translations.literal: Between Guide and Xuzhou there was a place called Zhujia Factory; local bandits held it and raided from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Between Guide and Xuzhou lay a place called Zhujia Factory, held by local bandits who sallied out to plunder whenever they could.

sentences.zh: 爌剿滅之。

translations.literal: Huang exterminated them.
translations.idiomatic: Huang wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 賊犯固始，大典檄爌及遊擊張士儀等分戍霍兵西南，扼賊東下，賊遂走六安。

translations.literal: When bandits invaded Gushi, Dadian ordered Huang and mobile corps commander Zhang Shiyi and others to divide forces and garrison southwest of Huoqiu, blocking the bandits' eastward advance; the bandits then fled toward Lu'an.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels invaded Gushi, Dadian dispatched Huang and mobile corps commander Zhang Shiyi and others to split their forces and hold positions southwest of Huoqiu, cutting off the enemy's eastward drive; the rebels then fled toward Lu'an.

sentences.zh: 大典又移爌等駐壽州東，兼護二陵。

translations.literal: Dadian then shifted Huang and the others to encamp east of Shouzhou, concurrently protecting the two imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Dadian then moved Huang and his men to a camp east of Shouzhou, with the added duty of guarding the two imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 當是時，長、淮南北，專以陵寢為重。

translations.literal: At that time, north and south of the Yangtze and Huai, priority was given exclusively to the imperial mausoleums.
translations.idiomatic: In those years, from the Yangtze to the Huai and on both banks, defense of the imperial tombs took precedence over everything else.

sentences.zh: 爌馳驅數年，幸無失事。

translations.literal: Huang galloped about for several years and fortunately met with no mishap.
translations.idiomatic: Huang rode hard from post to post for years and, by good fortune, never failed in his charge.

sentences.zh: 十二年六月擢總兵官，鎮守天津。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twelfth year he was promoted to regional commander and posted to guard Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twelfth year he was promoted to regional commander and assigned to guard Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 久之，移鎮甘肅。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to command Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was transferred to command Gansu.

sentences.zh: 十五年督三協副將王世寵、王加春、魯胤昌等討破叛番，斬首七百余級，撫安三十八族而還。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he directed the three assistant deputy commanders Wang Shichong, Wang Jiachun, Lu Yinchang, and others to campaign against and defeat rebel tribes, cut off more than seven hundred heads, pacified thirty-eight clans, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he led assistant deputy commanders Wang Shichong, Wang Jiachun, Lu Yinchang, and others against rebel tribes, took more than seven hundred heads, pacified thirty-eight clans, and returned in triumph.

sentences.zh: 其冬，督師孫傳庭檄召不至，疏劾之。

translations.literal: That winter, supreme commander Sun Chuanting summoned him by dispatch but he did not come; Chuanting memorialized impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: That winter supreme commander Sun Chuanting summoned him by dispatch, but Huang failed to appear; Chuanting then impeached him in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝令察爌堪辦賊，許戴罪圖功，否即以賜劍從事。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered an investigation into whether Huang was capable of handling the bandits, permitting him to redeem his guilt through merit; otherwise he would be dealt with by the gift sword.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an inquiry into whether Huang was fit to fight the rebels, allowing him to redeem his guilt through service—or else face execution by the imperial sword.

sentences.zh: 及爌至軍，傳庭貸其罪。

translations.literal: When Huang reached the army, Chuanting pardoned his offense.
translations.idiomatic: Once Huang reached the camp, Chuanting remitted his punishment.

sentences.zh: 已，復以逗留淫掠被劾，帝仍令載罪自效。

translations.literal: Before long he was again impeached for lingering and rapacious plunder; the emperor still ordered him to carry his guilt and redeem himself through service.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was impeached again for dawdling and allowing his men to plunder at will, yet the emperor still ordered him to serve on, bearing his guilt until he could prove himself.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，傳庭將出關。

translations.literal: The following autumn, Chuanting was about to march out of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: The next autumn Chuanting prepared to lead his army out through the pass.

sentences.zh: 有傳賊自內鄉窺商、雒者，檄爌移商州扼其北犯。

translations.literal: There were reports that bandits from Neixiang were watching Shang and Luo; he dispatched Huang to move to Shangzhou to block their northward invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that rebels from Neixiang were probing toward Shang and Luo; Chuanting ordered Huang to shift to Shangzhou and block their northward thrust.

sentences.zh: 已而傳庭師覆，爌遂還鎮。

translations.literal: Before long Chuanting's army was destroyed; Huang then returned to his command post.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting's army was soon destroyed, and Huang returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊陷延綏、寧夏，遂陷蘭州，渡河抵甘州還攻之。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits captured Yan'an and Ningxia, then captured Lanzhou, crossed the river and reached Ganzhou, then turned back to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels took Yan'an and Ningxia, then Lanzhou; they crossed the river, reached Ganzhou, and turned back to besiege the city.

sentences.zh: 爌與巡撫林日瑞竭力固守。

translations.literal: Huang and Grand Coordinator Lin Rirui exerted themselves to the utmost in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Huang and Grand Coordinator Lin Rirui strained every resource to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 賊乘雪夜坎而登。

translations.literal: The bandits took advantage of a snowy night to dig through and climb the walls.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels used a snowy night to undermine the wall and scale it.

sentences.zh: 士卒寒甚，不能戰，城遂陷。

translations.literal: The soldiers were exceedingly cold and could not fight; the city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were frozen stiff and could not fight; the city fell.

sentences.zh: 爌、日瑞及中軍哈維新、姚世儒皆死焉。

translations.literal: Huang, Rirui, and staff officers Ha Weixin and Yao Shiru all died there.
translations.idiomatic: Huang, Lin Rirui, and staff officers Ha Weixin and Yao Shiru all perished in the fall.

sentences.zh: 弟飈為沔陽州同知，城陷，亦死之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Biao served as subprefectural judge of Mianyang; when the city fell, he also died for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Biao, serving as subprefectural judge of Mianyang, also died when the city fell.

sentences.zh: 爌父子兄弟並死國難。

translations.literal: The Lin father, sons, and brothers alike all died in the state's crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Father, sons, and brothers of the Lin family alike perished in the nation's calamity.

sentences.zh: 何卿，成都衛人。

translations.literal: He Qing was a native of the Chengdu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He Qing was a native of the Chengdu Guard.

sentences.zh: 有誌操，習武事。

translations.literal: He had resolute character and was versed in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of firm principle and well trained in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 正德中，嗣世職為指揮僉事。

translations.literal: During the Zhengde reign he inherited the hereditary post as assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he inherited his family's post as assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 以能，擢筠連守備。

translations.literal: For his ability he was promoted to garrison commander of Junlian.
translations.idiomatic: On account of his ability he was promoted to garrison commander of Junlian.

sentences.zh: 從巡撫盛應期擊斬叛賊謝文禮、文義。

translations.literal: Following Grand Coordinator Sheng Yingqi he attacked and beheaded the rebel bandits Xie Wenli and Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Grand Coordinator Sheng Yingqi, he attacked and killed the rebel leaders Xie Wenli and Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，論功，進署都指揮僉事，充左參將，協守松潘。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended, merits were assessed; he was advanced to acting assistant regional commander, appointed left assistant commander, and jointly guarded Songpan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, merits were reckoned; Qing was promoted to acting assistant regional commander, made left assistant commander, and assigned to help guard Songpan.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，芒部土舍隴政、土婦支祿等叛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing, the Mangbu tribal head Long Zheng, the tribal woman Zhi Lu, and others rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign the Mangbu chieftain Long Zheng, the tribal woman Zhi Lu, and their followers rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 卿討之，斬首二百余級，降其眾數百人。

translations.literal: Qing campaigned against them, cut off more than two hundred heads, and brought several hundred of their followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Qing marched against them, took more than two hundred heads, and brought several hundred of their followers to surrender.

sentences.zh: 政奔烏撒，卿檄土官安寧擒以獻。

translations.literal: Zheng fled to Wusa; Qing dispatched orders to the tribal officer An Ning to capture him and present him.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng fled to Wusa, and Qing ordered the tribal officer An Ning to seize him and deliver him up.

sentences.zh: 寧佯諾，而匿政不出。

translations.literal: Ning pretended to agree but concealed Zheng and did not produce him.
translations.idiomatic: An Ning feigned agreement but hid Zheng and refused to hand him over.

sentences.zh: 巡撫湯沐言狀，帝奪卿冠帶。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Tang Mu reported the situation; the emperor stripped Qing of his official hat and belt.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Tang Mu reported what had happened, and the emperor stripped Qing of his rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 川、貴兵合討，賊始滅，還冠帶如初。

translations.literal: Sichuan and Guizhou troops jointly campaigned; the bandits were finally exterminated, and his hat and belt were restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan and Guizhou forces campaigned together until the rebels were wiped out, and Qing's rank insignia was restored.

sentences.zh: 五年春擢卿副總兵，仍鎮松潘。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year he was promoted to deputy regional commander, still commanding Songpan.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year he was promoted to deputy regional commander and continued to command Songpan.

sentences.zh: 隴氏已絕，改芒部為鎮雄府，設流官。

translations.literal: The Long clan was extinct; Mangbu was changed to Zhenxiong Prefecture and regular officials were installed.
translations.idiomatic: With the Long line extinguished, Mangbu was reorganized as Zhenxiong Prefecture and placed under appointed civil officials.

sentences.zh: 未幾，政遺黨沙保復叛。

translations.literal: Before long, remnant followers of Zheng led by Sha Bao rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zheng's remaining partisans, led by Sha Bao, rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 卿偕參將魏武、參議姚汝臯等並進，斬保等賊首七人，余盡殄。

translations.literal: Qing together with Assistant Commander Wei Wu, Administrative Commissioner Yao Rugao, and others advanced together, beheaded seven bandit chiefs including Bao, and exterminated the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Qing advanced with Assistant Commander Wei Wu, Administrative Commissioner Yao Rugao, and others, beheaded seven rebel leaders including Sha Bao, and annihilated the rest.

sentences.zh: 錄功，武最，卿次之，賜賚有差。

translations.literal: Merits were recorded—Wu ranked first, Qing second; rewards were granted in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: When merits were recorded, Wei Wu ranked first and Qing second; both received imperial rewards in due measure.

sentences.zh: 黑虎五砦番反，圍長安諸堡，烏都、鵓鴿諸番亦繼叛。

translations.literal: The Heihu Five Stockade tribes rebelled and besieged the forts of Chang'an; the Wudu and Boge tribes also rebelled in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Heihu Five Stockade tribes rose up and besieged the forts around Chang'an, and the Wudu and Boge tribes rebelled in turn.

sentences.zh: 卿皆破平之，就進都督僉事。

translations.literal: Qing defeated and pacified them all, and was thereupon promoted to assistant regional commander of the central military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Qing defeated and pacified them all and was promptly promoted to assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 威茂番十余砦連兵劫軍餉，且攻茂州及長寧諸堡，要撫賞。

translations.literal: More than ten stockades of the Weimao tribes joined forces to plunder army provisions, and moreover attacked Maozhou and the forts of Changning, demanding pacification rewards.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten Weimao stockades joined forces to raid army supplies and attack Maozhou and the forts of Changning, demanding pacification payments.

sentences.zh: 卿與副使朱紈築茂州外城以困之。

translations.literal: Qing together with Vice Commissioner Zhu Wan built the outer wall of Maozhou to hem them in.
translations.idiomatic: Qing and Vice Commissioner Zhu Wan built an outer wall around Maozhou to pin the rebels down.

sentences.zh: 旋以計殘其眾，戰屢捷，遂攻深溝，焚其碉砦。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward by stratagem he crippled their forces; battles were repeatedly victorious; he then attacked Shengou and burned their blockhouses and stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He soon crippled their strength by stratagem, won battle after battle, stormed Shengou, and burned their blockhouses and stockades.

sentences.zh: 諸番窘，請贖罪。

translations.literal: The tribes were distressed and requested to atone for their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, the tribes asked to submit and atone for their crimes.

sentences.zh: 卿責獻首惡，番不應。

translations.literal: Qing demanded they surrender the ringleaders; the tribes did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Qing demanded the ringleaders be handed over, but the tribes refused.

sentences.zh: 復分剿淺溝、渾水二砦殲之。

translations.literal: He again divided forces to suppress and annihilate the two stockades of Qiankou and Hunshui.
translations.idiomatic: He then split his forces and wiped out the two stockades at Qiankou and Hunshui.

sentences.zh: 諸番乃爭獻首惡，插血斷指耳，誓不復叛。

translations.literal: The tribes then competed to surrender the ringleaders, inserting blood and severing fingers as oath, vowing never to rebel again.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes then vied to deliver up the ringleaders, swearing blood oaths and severing fingers to vow they would never rebel again.

sentences.zh: 卿乃與刻木為約，分處其曹，畫疆守，松潘路復通。

translations.literal: Qing then carved wood to make a covenant, distributed their groups, drew boundaries for defense, and the Songpan route was restored to passage.
translations.idiomatic: Qing carved their pact into wood, resettled the tribes by group, fixed boundaries for each to hold, and the road to Songpan was open once more.

sentences.zh: 巡撫潘鑒等上二人功，詔賚銀幣，進署都督同知，鎮守如故。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Pan Jian and others memorialized the merits of the two men; the emperor ordered silver and silks bestowed, and Qing was advanced to acting regional vice commander, guarding as before.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Pan Jian and others reported the achievements of the two commanders; the court bestowed silver and silks, and Qing was promoted to acting regional vice commander while retaining his command.

sentences.zh: 久之，以疾致仕。

translations.literal: After a long time he retired due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: In time he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，塞上多警。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year there were many alarms on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year alarms multiplied along the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 召卿，以疾辭。

translations.literal: Qing was summoned but declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned him, but he declined on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，奪其都督，命以都指揮使詣部聽調。

translations.literal: The emperor was angered, stripped him of his regional commander rank, and ordered him to proceed to the ministry as regional commander to await assignment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged, stripped him of his regional commander's rank, and ordered him to report to the ministry as a regional commander awaiting orders.

sentences.zh: 未幾，寇逼畿輔，命營盧溝橋。

translations.literal: Before long invaders pressed the capital region; he was ordered to encamp at Lugou Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Before long raiders threatened the capital region, and he was ordered to encamp at Lugou Bridge.

sentences.zh: 松潘副總兵李爵為巡撫丘養浩劾罷，詔以卿代。

translations.literal: Songpan deputy regional commander Li Jue was impeached and dismissed by Grand Coordinator Qiu Yanghao; the emperor ordered Qing to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Songpan deputy regional commander Li Jue was impeached and removed by Grand Coordinator Qiu Yanghao, and the emperor ordered Qing to take his place.

sentences.zh: 給事中許天倫言卿賄養浩劾爵，自為地。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Xu Tianlun said Qing bribed Yanghao to impeach Jue, clearing ground for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Xu Tianlun charged that Qing had bribed Qiu Yanghao to impeach Li Jue and clear the way for his own appointment.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，褫卿及養浩官，令巡按冉崇禮核實。

translations.literal: The emperor was angered, stripped Qing and Yanghao of their offices, and ordered Investigating Censor Ran Chongli to verify the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, stripped both Qing and Qiu Yanghao of their posts, and ordered Investigating Censor Ran Chongli to investigate.

sentences.zh: 時兵事棘，翁萬達復薦卿，還其都督僉事，都東官廳軍馬。

translations.literal: At the time military affairs were critical; Weng Wanda again recommended Qing, restored his rank as assistant regional commander, and assigned him the troops and horses of the Eastern Official Hall.
translations.idiomatic: With military affairs pressing, Weng Wanda recommended Qing again; his rank as assistant regional commander was restored and he was put in charge of the Eastern Official Hall troops.

sentences.zh: 已而崇禮具言爵貪汙，「卿鎮松潘十七年，為蜀保障，軍民頌德，且貧，安所得賄？」

translations.literal: Before long Chongli fully reported that Jue was greedy and corrupt: "Qing has commanded Songpan for seventeen years as Sichuan's bulwark; soldiers and civilians praise his virtue, and he is moreover poor—whence could he obtain bribes?"
translations.idiomatic: Ran Chongli then reported in full that Li Jue was corrupt: "Qing has held Songpan for seventeen years as the shield of Shu; soldiers and civilians praise his virtue, and he is poor besides—where would he find money for bribes?"

sentences.zh: 帝意乃解。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was then eased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger subsided.

sentences.zh: 四川白草番為亂，副總兵高岡鳳被劾。

translations.literal: The Baicao tribes of Sichuan revolted; deputy regional commander Gao Gangfeng was impeached.
translations.idiomatic: When the Baicao tribes of Sichuan rose in revolt, deputy regional commander Gao Gangfeng was impeached.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書路迎奏卿代之。

translations.literal: Minister of War Lu Ying memorialized that Qing should replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Lu Ying memorialized that Qing should replace him.

sentences.zh: 卿再蒞松潘，將士鹹喜。

translations.literal: Qing came again to Songpan; officers and soldiers were all delighted.
translations.idiomatic: When Qing returned to Songpan, officers and soldiers alike rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 乃會巡撫張時徹討擒渠惡數人，俘斬九百七十有奇，克營砦四十七，毀碉房四千八百，獲馬牛器械儲積各萬計。

translations.literal: He then joined Grand Coordinator Zhang Shiche in campaigning, capturing and beheading several ringleaders, taking and killing nine hundred seventy-odd enemies, capturing forty-seven camp stockades, destroying four thousand eight hundred blockhouse dwellings, and seizing horses, cattle, weapons, and stored goods numbering in the tens of thousands each.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Grand Coordinator Zhang Shiche in a campaign that captured several ringleaders, killed more than nine hundred seventy of the enemy, took forty-seven camp stockades, destroyed four thousand eight hundred blockhouse dwellings, and seized horses, cattle, weapons, and stores by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 進署都督同知。

translations.literal: He was advanced to acting regional vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting regional vice commander.

sentences.zh: 卿素有威望，為番人所憚。

translations.literal: Qing had long enjoyed prestige and was feared by the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Qing had long commanded respect, and the tribes feared him.

sentences.zh: 自威茂迄松潘、龍安夾道築墻數百里，行旌往來，無剽奪患。

translations.literal: From Weimao to Songpan and Long'an, walled fortifications were built for several hundred li along the route; traveling banners came and went without the affliction of plunder.
translations.idiomatic: From Weimao through Songpan to Long'an, walls were built for hundreds of li along the road, and travelers passed without fear of robbery.

sentences.zh: 先後蒞鎮二十四年，軍民戴之若慈母。

translations.literal: Over twenty-four years of command in all, soldiers and civilians revered him as they would a loving mother.
translations.idiomatic: Across twenty-four years of command, soldiers and civilians honored him as they would a devoted mother.

sentences.zh: 再以疾歸。

translations.literal: He again retired due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: He retired again on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，倭寇海上。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, Japanese pirates raided the coast.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year Japanese pirates raided the coast.

sentences.zh: 詔卿與沈希儀各率家眾赴蘇、松軍門。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Qing and Shen Xiyi each to lead their household troops to the Suzhou-Songjiang military headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Qing and Shen Xiyi each to lead their household troops to the Suzhou-Songjiang military headquarters.

sentences.zh: 明年充副總兵，總理浙江及蘇、松海防。

translations.literal: The following year he served as deputy regional commander, overseeing coastal defense for Zhejiang and Suzhou-Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he served as deputy regional commander with overall charge of coastal defense in Zhejiang and the Suzhou-Songjiang region.

sentences.zh: 卿，蜀中名將，不諳海道，年已老，兵與將不習，竟不能有所為。

translations.literal: Qing was a famous general of Shu but unversed in sea routes; he was already old, and troops and commanders were unfamiliar with each other—ultimately he could accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was a celebrated general of Shu, but he knew nothing of sea warfare; he was already old, and his troops and officers were strangers to one another—in the end he achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 為巡按御史周如鬥劾罷，卒。

translations.literal: He was impeached and dismissed by Investigating Censor Zhou Rudou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Zhou Rudou impeached and removed him; he died soon after.

sentences.zh: 沈希儀，字唐佐，貴縣人。

translations.literal: Shen Xiyi, style name Tangzuo, was a native of Guixian.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Xiyi, styled Tangzuo, was a native of Guixian.

sentences.zh: 嗣世職為奉議衛指揮使。

translations.literal: He inherited the hereditary post as commander of the Fengyi Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his family's post as commander of the Fengyi Guard.

sentences.zh: 機警有膽勇，智計過絕於人。

translations.literal: He was alert and possessed courage; his ingenuity surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and bold, his resourcefulness was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年，調征永安。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhengde he was transferred for the campaign at Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of the Zhengde reign he was transferred to the Yong'an campaign.

sentences.zh: 以數百人搗陳村砦，馬陷淖中，騰而上，連馘三酋，破其余眾。

translations.literal: Leading several hundred men he stormed Chencun Stockade; his horse sank in mud but he leaped up and continued, severing three chieftains' heads in succession and routing the rest.
translations.idiomatic: At the head of several hundred men he stormed Chencun Stockade; when his horse sank in the mire he sprang free, cut down three chieftains in succession, and routed the rest.

sentences.zh: 進署都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to acting assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 義寧賊寇臨桂，還巢，希儀追之。

translations.literal: Bandits from Yining raided Lingui, then returned to their lair; Xiyi pursued them.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits from Yining raided Lingui and withdrew to their lair, Xiyi pursued them.

sentences.zh: 巢有兩隘，賊伏兵其一，使熟瑤紿官兵入。

translations.literal: The lair had two passes; the bandits hid troops at one and had assimilated Yao deceive the government troops into entering.
translations.idiomatic: The lair had two passes. The bandits lay in ambush at one of them and sent assimilated Yao to lure the government troops inside.

sentences.zh: 希儀策其詐，急從別隘直抵賊巢。

translations.literal: Xiyi guessed their trick and hastily took the other pass straight to the bandits' lair.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi saw through the ruse and hurried by the other pass straight to the bandits' lair.

sentences.zh: 賊倉卒還救，遂大破之。

translations.literal: The bandits rushed back in haste to rescue it and were thereupon routed.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits rushed back to defend their lair in disarray, and he routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 荔浦賊八千渡江東掠，希儀率五百人駐白面砦，待其歸。

translations.literal: Eight thousand bandits from Lipu crossed the river to raid eastward; Xiyi led five hundred men to garrison Baimian Stockade and wait for their return.
translations.idiomatic: When eight thousand Lipu bandits crossed the river to raid the east, Xiyi took five hundred men to hold Baimian Stockade and wait for them to come back.

sentences.zh: 砦去蛟龍、滑石兩灘各數里。

translations.literal: The stockade was several li from each of the two fords, Jiaolong and Huashi.
translations.idiomatic: The stockade stood several li from each of two fords, Jiaolong and Huashi.

sentences.zh: 希儀以滑石灘狹，雖眾可薄，蛟龍灘廣，濟則難圖，欲誘致之滑石。

translations.literal: Xiyi reasoned that Huashi Ford was narrow and even a large force could be pressed there, while Jiaolong Ford was broad and once they crossed it would be hard to attack; he wished to lure them to Huashi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi judged that Huashi Ford was narrow enough that even a large force could be pressed and overwhelmed there, whereas Jiaolong Ford was wide and once the bandits crossed it would be hard to strike; he meant to lure them to Huashi.

sentences.zh: 乃樹旗百蛟龍灘，守以羸卒，然柴以疑之。

translations.literal: He then planted a hundred flags at Jiaolong Ford, garrisoned it with weak troops, and burned firewood to create suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: He planted a hundred banners at Jiaolong Ford, left a thin garrison there, and lit fires to make the enemy suspect a trap.

sentences.zh: 賊果趨滑石。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed hurried to Huashi.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits duly made for Huashi.

sentences.zh: 希儀預以小艦載勁卒伏葭葦中。

translations.literal: Xiyi had beforehand loaded picked troops on small boats and hidden them among the reeds.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi had already hidden picked troops aboard small boats in the reeds.

sentences.zh: 賊渡且半，乘瀧急沖之，兩岸軍噪而前，賊眾多墜水死，收所掠而還。

translations.literal: When the bandits were halfway across, he seized the swift current to charge them; troops on both banks shouted and advanced, many bandits fell into the water and died, and he recovered what had been plundered and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits were half across, he struck with the current at full speed while troops on both banks shouted and pressed forward. Many bandits drowned; he recovered the plunder and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 從副總兵張祐連破臨桂、灌陽、古田賊。

translations.literal: Following deputy regional commander Zhang You, he repeatedly defeated bandits at Lingui, Guanyang, and Gutian.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Deputy Regional Commander Zhang You, he broke bandit forces at Lingui, Guanyang, and Gutian in succession.

sentences.zh: 進署都指揮同知，掌都司事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to acting regional assistant commander and took charge of the regional commander's office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting regional assistant commander and put in charge of the regional military administration.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年，總督姚鏌將討田州岑猛。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiajing, Grand Coordinator Yao Mo was about to campaign against Cen Meng of Tianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Jiajing reign, Grand Coordinator Yao Mo prepared to campaign against Cen Meng of Tianzhou.

sentences.zh: 用希儀計，間猛婦翁歸順土酋岑璋，使圖猛，而分兵五哨進。

translations.literal: Using Xiyi's plan, he estranged Meng's father-in-law, the Guishun chieftain Cen Zhang, and had him plot against Meng, while dividing the army into five columns to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Following Xiyi's plan, he turned Meng's father-in-law, the Guishun chieftain Cen Zhang, against him and sent the army forward in five columns.

sentences.zh: 希儀將中哨，當工堯。

translations.literal: Xiyi commanded the central column, facing Gongyao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi led the central column against Gongyao.

sentences.zh: 工堯，賊要地，聚眾守之。

translations.literal: Gongyao was a bandit strongpoint; they gathered a host to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyao was a key bandit position, and they massed troops to hold it.

sentences.zh: 希儀夜遣軍三百人，緣山上，繞出其背。

translations.literal: Xiyi by night sent three hundred troops up the mountain to circle behind them.
translations.idiomatic: That night Xiyi sent three hundred men up the mountain to get behind the enemy.

sentences.zh: 比明合戰，則所遣軍已立幟山巔，賊大潰敗。

translations.literal: By dawn when battle joined, the troops he had sent had already raised banners on the mountain crest, and the bandits were utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak, as the battle opened, his detachment was already planting banners on the summit; the bandits broke and fled in complete defeat.

sentences.zh: 猛走歸順，為璋所執，田州平。

translations.literal: Meng fled to Guishun and was seized by Zhang; Tianzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Meng fled to Guishun, where Zhang captured him, and Tianzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 希儀功最，鏌抑之，止受賚。

translations.literal: Xiyi's merit was greatest, but Mo suppressed it and he received only rewards of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xiyi's achievement was greatest, Mo downplayed it and he received only an imperial gift.

sentences.zh: 鏌議設流官，希儀曰：「思恩以流官故，亂至今未已。

translations.literal: Mo proposed establishing direct officials; Xiyi said, "Because of direct officials in Si'en, disorder has continued to the present without end.
translations.idiomatic: When Mo proposed appointing direct officials, Xiyi said, "Si'en has been in turmoil ever since direct officials were installed.

sentences.zh: 田州復然，兩賊且合從起。」

translations.literal: If Tianzhou follows suit, the two bandit forces will soon rise in alliance."
translations.idiomatic: If Tianzhou goes the same way, the two rebel groups will join forces and rise again.

sentences.zh: 鏌不從。

translations.literal: Mo did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Mo would not listen.

sentences.zh: 以希儀為右參將，分守思、田。

translations.literal: Xiyi was made right assistant general with divided duty guarding Si and Tian.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi was appointed right assistant general with divided responsibility for Si'en and Tianzhou.

sentences.zh: 希儀請還鄉治裝。

translations.literal: Xiyi requested to return home to prepare his gear.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi asked to go home and prepare his equipment.

sentences.zh: 以參將張經代守。

translations.literal: Assistant General Zhang Jing was put in his place to hold the post.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant General Zhang Jing was left to hold the garrison in his stead.

sentences.zh: 甫一月，田州復叛，鏌罷歸。

translations.literal: Barely a month later Tianzhou rebelled again, and Mo was dismissed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a month later Tianzhou rebelled again; Mo was removed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 王守仁代，多用希儀計，思、田復定。

translations.literal: Wang Shouren replaced him and made much use of Xiyi's plans; Si and Tian were again settled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouren took his place, relied heavily on Xiyi's plans, and pacified Si'en and Tianzhou once more.

sentences.zh: 改右江柳慶參將，駐柳州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right assistant general of Youjiang and Liuqing, garrisoned at Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as assistant general of the Youjiang and Liuqing circuit and stationed at Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 象州、武宣、融縣瑤反，討破之。

translations.literal: The Yao of Xiangzhou, Wuxuan, and Rongxian rebelled, and he campaigned and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yao of Xiangzhou, Wuxuan, and Rongxian rose in revolt, he defeated them in campaign.

sentences.zh: 謝病歸，頃之還故任。

translations.literal: He retired citing illness, and shortly afterward returned to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on grounds of illness, but before long resumed his former command.

sentences.zh: 柳在萬山中，城外五里即賊巢，軍民至無地可田，而官軍素罷不任戰。

translations.literal: Liuzhou lay amid myriad mountains; five li outside the walls were bandit lairs, soldiers and civilians had nowhere to farm, and the government troops had long been slack and unfit for battle.
translations.idiomatic: Liuzhou sat deep in the mountains; bandit lairs lay only five li beyond the walls, soldiers and civilians had no land safe enough to farm, and the government troops had long been slack and unfit for fighting.

sentences.zh: 又賊耳目遍官府，閨闥動靜無不知。

translations.literal: Moreover the bandits' eyes and ears filled the yamen; no movement within the inner quarters went unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit informants had infiltrated the yamen, and nothing that happened even in the inner quarters escaped their notice.

sentences.zh: 希儀謂欲大破賊，非狼兵不可，請於制府。

translations.literal: Xiyi said that to break the bandits decisively Lang troops were indispensable, and he requested them from the governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi argued that only Lang troops could break the bandits for good and asked the governor-general for them.

sentences.zh: 調那地狼兵二千來，戍兵稍振。

translations.literal: Two thousand Lang troops from Nadi were transferred there, and the garrison troops were somewhat revived.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand Lang troops from Nadi were sent up, and the garrison's morale improved.

sentences.zh: 乃求得與瑤通販易者數十人，持其罪而厚撫之，使诇賊。

translations.literal: He then found several dozen men who traded with the Yao, held their crimes over them yet treated them generously, and had them spy on the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He found several dozen men who traded with the Yao, held their offenses over them while treating them well, and turned them into spies.

sentences.zh: 賊動靜，希儀亦無不知。

translations.literal: Of the bandits' movements, Xiyi too knew nothing that he did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xiyi knew every move the bandits made.

sentences.zh: 希儀每出兵，雖肘腋親近不得聞。

translations.literal: Whenever Xiyi took the field, even those closest at his side were not told.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xiyi marched out, not even his closest aides were told beforehand.

sentences.zh: 至期鳴號，則諸軍咸集。

translations.literal: When the appointed time came he sounded the signal, and all the troops gathered.
translations.idiomatic: At the appointed hour he sounded the call, and the troops assembled at once.

sentences.zh: 令一人挾旗引諸軍行，不測所往。

translations.literal: He ordered one man carrying a banner to lead the troops on the march, with no one able to guess where they were going.
translations.idiomatic: He had one man carry a banner and lead the column, with no one knowing where they were bound.

sentences.zh: 及駐軍設伏，賊必至，遇伏輒奔。

translations.literal: When he halted the army and set ambushes, the bandits always came and, meeting ambush, always fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he halted to lay ambushes, the bandits always appeared—and always broke and ran when they struck the trap.

sentences.zh: 官軍擊之，無不如誌。

translations.literal: When government troops struck them, nothing ever failed to go as planned.
translations.idiomatic: Government attacks never failed to go as he intended.

sentences.zh: 已，賊寇他所，官軍又先至。

translations.literal: Later, when bandits raided some other place, government troops had already arrived first.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits struck elsewhere, government troops were already there waiting.

sentences.zh: 遠村僻聚，賊度官軍所不逮者，往寇之，官軍又未嘗不在，賊驚以為神。

translations.literal: In distant villages and secluded settlements where bandits judged government troops could not reach, they went to raid, yet government troops were never absent; the bandits were astonished and thought it supernatural.
translations.idiomatic: Even in remote hamlets the bandits thought beyond government reach, troops were waiting when they arrived. The bandits came to believe Xiyi was uncanny.

sentences.zh: 希儀得賊巢婦女畜產，果鄰巢者悉還之，惟取陰助賊者。

translations.literal: When Xiyi seized women, livestock, and goods from bandit lairs, he returned them all to neighboring lairs and took only those who had secretly aided the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When he captured women, livestock, and goods from a bandit lair, he returned everything to neighboring settlements and kept only those who had secretly helped the bandits.

sentences.zh: 諸瑤盡詟伏，無敢向賊。

translations.literal: All the Yao were thoroughly cowed and dared not turn toward the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao were thoroughly cowed and no longer dared aid the bandits.

sentences.zh: 希儀初至，令熟瑤得出入城中，無所禁。

translations.literal: When Xiyi first arrived, he allowed assimilated Yao to enter and leave the city without restriction.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiyi first arrived, he allowed assimilated Yao free passage in and out of the city.

sentences.zh: 因厚賞其黠者，使為諜。

translations.literal: He then richly rewarded the clever among them and made them spies.
translations.idiomatic: He richly rewarded the sharpest among them and turned them into spies.

sentences.zh: 後漸令瑤婦入見其妻，賚以酒食繒帛。

translations.literal: Later he gradually had Yao women come in to see his wife and bestowed wine, food, silk, and cloth on them.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually he had Yao women visit his wife and rewarded them with food, wine, silk, and cloth.

sentences.zh: 其夫常以賊情告者，則陰厚之。

translations.literal: If their husbands often reported bandit intelligence, he secretly rewarded them generously.
translations.idiomatic: When their husbands brought word of the bandits, he secretly rewarded the families well.

sentences.zh: 諸瑤婦利賞，爭勸其夫輸賊情，或自入府言之。

translations.literal: The Yao women, coveting the rewards, all urged their husbands to deliver bandit intelligence, or entered the yamen themselves to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy for the rewards, Yao women urged their husbands to report on the bandits or came to the yamen themselves with news.

sentences.zh: 以故，賊益無所匿形。

translations.literal: For this reason the bandits increasingly had nowhere to hide their forms.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this the bandits had nowhere left to hide.

sentences.zh: 希儀每於風雨晦冥夜，偵賊所止宿，分遣人賫銃潛伏舍旁。

translations.literal: Xiyi often on nights of wind, rain, and murk tracked where bandits lodged, sent men carrying muskets to lie hidden beside their dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: On dark, stormy nights Xiyi would locate where the bandits were sleeping and send men with muskets to hide beside their houses.

sentences.zh: 中夜銃舉，賊大駭曰：「老沈來矣！」

translations.literal: At midnight the muskets fired; the bandits were greatly terrified and cried, "Old Shen has come!"
translations.idiomatic: At midnight the muskets cracked; the bandits cried in terror, "Old Shen is here!

sentences.zh: 鹹挈妻子匍匐上山。

translations.literal: All dragged wives and children and crawled up the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: They grabbed their wives and children and crawled up the mountainside.

sentences.zh: 兒啼女號，或寒凍觸厓石死，爭怨悔作賊非計。

translations.literal: Babies wailed and women screamed; some died from cold and frost striking cliff rocks; all regretted and complained that becoming bandits had been no plan.
translations.idiomatic: Children wailed and women screamed; some froze to death against the cliffs; all cursed the life of banditry they had chosen.

sentences.zh: 至曉下山，則寂無人聲。

translations.literal: When at dawn they came down the mountain, there was silence and no human voice.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak they came down the mountain to find nothing but silence.

sentences.zh: 他巢亦然，眾愈益驚。

translations.literal: Other lairs were the same; the crowd grew ever more alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The same thing happened at other lairs, and their fear only grew.

sentences.zh: 潛遣人入城偵之，則希儀故居城中不出也。

translations.literal: They secretly sent men into the city to spy, and Xiyi was still dwelling in the city and had not gone out.
translations.idiomatic: They secretly sent men to spy in the city and found Xiyi still at home, never having left.

sentences.zh: 賊膽落，多易面為熟瑤。

translations.literal: The bandits' courage fell away; many changed their appearance to become assimilated Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Their courage broke; many disguised themselves as assimilated Yao and gave up the life.

sentences.zh: 韋扶諫者，馬平瑤魁也，累捕不得。

translations.literal: Wei Fujian was a Yao chieftain of Maping; repeated captures failed to take him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Fujian was a Yao chieftain of Maping who had eluded capture again and again.

sentences.zh: 有報扶諫逃鄰賊三層巢者，希儀潛率兵剿之，則又與三層賊往劫他所。

translations.literal: When word came that Fujian had fled to the neighboring bandits' Sanceng lair, Xiyi secretly led troops to suppress it, but Fujian had again gone with the Sanceng bandits to raid elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Fujian had fled to the neighboring Sanceng lair, Xiyi led a secret raid—only to find that Fujian had already gone raiding elsewhere with the Sanceng bandits.

sentences.zh: 希儀盡俘三層巢妻子歸，希儀俘賊妻子盡以畀狼兵，至是獨閉之空舍，飲食之。

translations.literal: Xiyi captured all the wives and children of the Sanceng lair and brought them back; previously Xiyi had given all captured bandit wives and children to the Lang troops, but this time he alone shut them in empty houses and fed them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi took all the wives and children of the Sanceng lair captive. Before, he had handed captured families over to the Lang troops; this time he locked them in empty houses and fed them himself.

sentences.zh: 使熟瑤往語其夫曰：「得韋扶諫，還矣。」

translations.literal: He had assimilated Yao go tell their husbands, "If Wei Fujian is obtained, they will be returned."
translations.idiomatic: He sent assimilated Yao to tell the husbands, "Hand over Wei Fujian and your families will be returned.

sentences.zh: 諸瑤聞，悉來謁希儀。

translations.literal: All the Yao heard and came to pay respects to Xiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the Yao came in numbers to see Xiyi.

sentences.zh: 今入室視之，妻子固無恙。

translations.literal: When they now entered the rooms to look, wives and children were indeed unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: When they were allowed inside to look, their wives and children were indeed unharmed.

sentences.zh: 乃共誘扶諫出巢，縛以獻，易妻子還。

translations.literal: They then jointly lured Fujian out of the lair, bound him and presented him, and exchanged him for the return of wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Together they lured Fujian out of hiding, bound him, and handed him over in exchange for their families.

sentences.zh: 希儀剜扶諫目，支解之，懸諸城門。

translations.literal: Xiyi gouged out Fujian's eyes, dismembered him, and hung the pieces at the city gates.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi gouged out Fujian's eyes, dismembered him, and displayed the remains at the city gates.

sentences.zh: 諸瑤服希儀威信，益不敢為盜。

translations.literal: All the Yao submitted to Xiyi's prestige and authority and dared still less to become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao submitted to Xiyi's authority and no longer dared turn to banditry.

sentences.zh: 自是，柳城四旁數百里，無敢攘奪者。

translations.literal: From then on, for several hundred li around Liucheng, none dared plunder and seize.
translations.idiomatic: After that, for hundreds of li around Liucheng, no one dared rob or plunder.

sentences.zh: 希儀嘗上書於朝，言狼兵亦瑤、僮耳。

translations.literal: Xiyi once memorialized the court, saying Lang troops were also Yao and Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi once memorialized the court, observing that Lang troops were Yao and Zhuang like any other.

sentences.zh: 瑤、僮所在為賊，而狼兵死不敢為非，非狼兵順，而瑤、僮逆也。

translations.literal: Where Yao and Zhuang lived they became bandits, yet Lang troops would not dare do wrong even unto death; it was not that Lang troops were obedient while Yao and Zhuang were rebellious.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Zhuang where they lived under direct officials turned to banditry, while Lang troops would not dare misbehave even on pain of death—not because Lang troops were naturally obedient and Yao and Zhuang naturally rebellious.

sentences.zh: 狼兵隸土官，瑤、僮隸流官。

translations.literal: Lang troops were subject to native officials; Yao and Zhuang were subject to direct officials.
translations.idiomatic: Lang troops answered to native chiefs; Yao and Zhuang answered to direct officials.

sentences.zh: 土官令嚴足以制狼兵，流官勢輕不能制瑤、僮。

translations.literal: Native officials' commands were strict enough to control Lang troops; direct officials' authority was light and could not control Yao and Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Native chiefs ruled strictly enough to control Lang troops, but direct officials lacked the authority to control Yao and Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 若割瑤、僮分隸之旁近土官，土官世世富貴，不敢有他望。

translations.literal: If Yao and Zhuang were carved up and placed under nearby native officials, those native officials would be rich and noble generation after generation and would not dare harbor other ambitions.
