translations.idiomatic: If Yao and Zhuang territories were divided among neighboring native chiefs, those chiefs would remain wealthy and honored for generations and would not dare aspire to more.

sentences.zh: 以國家之力制土官，以土官之力制瑤、僮，皆為狼兵，兩廣世世無患矣。

translations.literal: Using the state's power to control native officials and native officials' power to control Yao and Zhuang, all would become like Lang troops, and the Two Guangs would be free of trouble generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: The state would control the native chiefs, the native chiefs would control the Yao and Zhuang, and all would serve like Lang troops—then Guangdong and Guangxi would know peace for generations.

sentences.zh: 時不能用。

translations.literal: At the time his plan could not be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not adopt his proposal.

sentences.zh: 至十六年而有思恩岑金之變。

translations.literal: By the sixteenth year there came the uprising of Cen Jin of Si'en.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year came the rebellion of Cen Jin of Si'en.

sentences.zh: 初，思恩土官岑浚既誅，改設流官，以其酋二人韋貴、徐五為土巡檢，分掌其兵各萬余。

translations.literal: At first, after the native official of Si'en, Cen Jun, was executed, direct officials were installed; two of his chieftains, Wei Gui and Xu Wu, were made native assistant inspectors, each commanding more than ten thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the Si'en native ruler Cen Jun was executed and direct officials were installed, two of his chiefs, Wei Gui and Xu Wu, were made native assistant inspectors, each commanding more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 夷民不樂漢法，凡數叛。

translations.literal: The tribal people did not delight in Han law and rebelled several times in all.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal peoples resented Han administration and rebelled repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 鎮安有男子名金，自言浚子。

translations.literal: In Zhen'an there was a man named Jin who declared himself Jun's son.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhen'an a man named Jin claimed to be Cen Jun's son.

sentences.zh: 鎮安土官乃潛召其舊部酋長，出金而與之盟曰：「若小主也。」

translations.literal: The native official of Zhen'an secretly summoned Jun's former subordinate chieftains, produced Jin, and swore an oath with them, saying, "This is the young lord."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhen'an native chief secretly summoned Jun's former subordinate chiefs, produced Jin, and swore them to him, saying, "This is your rightful lord.

sentences.zh: 諸酋羅拜，擁金歸，聚兵五千，將攻城，復故地，遠近洶洶。

translations.literal: The chieftains bowed in a circle, escorted Jin home, gathered five thousand troops, were about to storm the city and recover the old territory; near and far were in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: The chiefs bowed in homage, escorted Jin home, raised five thousand men, and prepared to storm the city and reclaim their old lands; alarm spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 浚誅時，其酋楊留者無所歸，率黨千余人詣賓州，應募為打手。

translations.literal: When Jun was executed, his chieftain Yang Liu had nowhere to go; he led more than a thousand followers to Binzhou and enlisted as brawlers.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun was executed, one of his chiefs, Yang Liu, had nowhere to go; he led more than a thousand followers to Binzhou and enlisted as mercenary fighters.

sentences.zh: 希儀在賓，留入言，欲往見小主人。

translations.literal: Xiyi was at Bin; Liu entered and spoke, wishing to go see the young master.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi was stationed at Binzhou when Liu came to him and said he wanted to go see the young lord.

sentences.zh: 希儀故患金，及聞留言，益大駭。

translations.literal: Xiyi had long been troubled by Jin, and on hearing Liu's words he was all the more greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi had already been worried about Jin, and Liu's words alarmed him still further.

sentences.zh: 因好謂留曰：「是岑浚第九子耶？

translations.literal: He therefore spoke kindly to Liu, saying, "Is this the ninth son of Cen Jun?
translations.idiomatic: He spoke warmly to Liu and asked, "Is this Cen Jun's ninth son?

sentences.zh: 我向征田州固聞之。」

translations.literal: When I campaigned against Tianzhou before I indeed heard of him."
translations.idiomatic: I heard of him when I campaigned in Tianzhou.

sentences.zh: 因自語：「岑氏其復乎？」

translations.literal: He then said to himself, "Will the Cen clan be restored?"
translations.idiomatic: Then, as if to himself, he murmured, "Will the Cen house rise again?

sentences.zh: 欲以深動留，留果喜。

translations.literal: Wishing to move Liu deeply, Liu was indeed delighted.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to stir Liu deeply, and Liu was delighted.

sentences.zh: 已，召留密室，言：「予我重賂，即為金復官。」

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he summoned Liu to a secret room and said, "Give me a heavy bribe and I will restore Jin's office for you."
translations.idiomatic: Then he drew Liu into a private room and said, "Bring me a rich reward and I will restore Jin to office.

sentences.zh: 且出，復呼入曰：「韋貴、徐五今分將思恩兵，必讎金，善防之。」

translations.literal: As Liu was leaving, he called him back in and said, "Wei Gui and Xu Wu now divide command of Si'en's troops; they are sure to bear enmity toward Jin—guard against them well."
translations.idiomatic: As Liu was leaving, he called him back and added, "Wei Gui and Xu Wu now command Si'en's forces between them; they will surely seek revenge on Jin—be on your guard.

sentences.zh: 留益大信。

translations.literal: Liu believed all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Liu believed him completely.

sentences.zh: 金遂從五千人因留以見。

translations.literal: Jin thereupon came with five thousand men following Liu to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then came with five thousand men, led by Liu, to see Xiyi.

sentences.zh: 門者奔告，請無納。

translations.literal: The gatekeeper ran to report and asked that they not be admitted.
translations.idiomatic: The gatekeeper ran in and urged that they not be admitted.

sentences.zh: 希儀罵曰：「金，土官子，非賊，奈何不納？」

translations.literal: Xiyi cursed and said, "Jin is a native official's son, not a bandit—why not admit him?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi rebuked him: "Jin is a native chief's son, not a bandit—why turn him away?

sentences.zh: 引入，厚結之，又引以詣兵備副使，隨以計漸散其五千人。

translations.literal: He had them brought in, treated Jin warmly and bonded with him, then led him to the vice commissioner for military affairs, and by stratagem gradually dispersed his five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He admitted them, treated Jin generously and won his trust, then escorted him to the vice commissioner for military affairs while gradually dispersing his five thousand followers by stratagem.

sentences.zh: 卒縛金，留亦自恨死，思恩復寧。

translations.literal: In the end Jin was bound; Liu also died of self-reproach, and Si'en was again settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Jin was bound; Liu died consumed by remorse, and Si'en was pacified once more.

sentences.zh: 已，從總督張經大破斷藤峽、弩灘賊，受賚歸。

translations.literal: Later, following Grand Coordinator Zhang Jing, he greatly defeated the bandits of Duanteng Gorge and Nudan, received rewards, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Later, serving under Grand Coordinator Zhang Jing, he routed the bandits of Duanteng Gorge and Nudan, received an imperial reward, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 希儀鎮柳、慶久，渠魁宿猾捕誅殆盡。

translations.literal: Xiyi garrisoned Liuzhou and Qing for a long time; ringleaders and hardened villains were captured and executed nearly to the last.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi held Liuzhou and Qing for many years, hunting down ringleaders and old hands until scarcely any remained.

sentences.zh: 先後搗巢，斬馘積五千余級，未嘗悉奏功，故多不敘。

translations.literal: Time and again he stormed their lairs, accumulating more than five thousand heads cut, yet never reported all his achievements, so many went unrewarded in the records.
translations.idiomatic: He raided their strongholds again and again, piling up more than five thousand enemy heads, but he never reported every victory—so much of his merit went unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 十九年復謝病，柳人祀之山雲祠。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he again pleaded illness; the people of Liuzhou enshrined him at the Shanyun Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he again retired on grounds of illness, and the people of Liuzhou honored him at the Shanyun Temple.

sentences.zh: 旋起四川左參將，分守敘、滬及貴州迤西諸處。

translations.literal: Soon after he was reappointed left vice commander of Sichuan, with divided defense of Xu, Lu, and the far western districts of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as left vice commander of Sichuan, charged with defending Xu, Luzhou, and the western reaches of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 其冬，擢署都督僉事，充總兵官，鎮貴州。

translations.literal: That winter he was promoted to acting assistant regional commander, appointed regional commander, and stationed at Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was elevated to acting assistant regional commander and appointed regional commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 復謝病歸。

translations.literal: Again he pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He again pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 塞上多警，召天下名將至京師，希儀在召中。

translations.literal: With many alarms on the northern frontier, famous generals from across the realm were summoned to the capital; Xiyi was among those called.
translations.idiomatic: Alarm piled upon alarm on the northern frontier, and famous generals from across the empire were summoned to the capital—Xiyi among them.

sentences.zh: 希儀鎮柳、慶，每戰必先登，身數被創，陰雨輒痛劇，故數謝病。

translations.literal: While garrisoning Liuzhou and Qing, Xiyi was first to scale the walls in every battle and was wounded many times; rainy weather brought severe pain, hence his repeated pleas of illness.
translations.idiomatic: At Liuzhou and Qing, Xiyi had always been the first man over the wall; he bore many wounds, and rainy days brought him agony—hence his many retirements on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 至京，亦以病辭。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital he likewise declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the capital, he too declined service on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 帝疑其規避，褫都督官，令赴部候用。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected evasion, stripped him of his regional commander's rank, and ordered him to report to the ministry awaiting appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected he was shirking duty, stripped him of his commander's rank, and ordered him to wait at the ministry for reassignment.

sentences.zh: 翁萬達薦其才。

translations.literal: Weng Wanda recommended his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda spoke up for his abilities.

sentences.zh: 會江、淮多盜，議設督捕總兵官，乃復希儀署都督僉事以往。

translations.literal: Just then banditry was rampant on the Yangtze and Huai, and a post of regional commander for bandit suppression was proposed; Xiyi was accordingly restored as acting assistant regional commander and sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry flared along the Yangtze and Huai, and the court proposed a regional commander to hunt them down; Xiyi was restored as acting assistant regional commander and sent to take the post.

sentences.zh: 二十六年以為廣東副總兵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was made deputy regional commander of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed deputy regional commander of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 命自今將領至自川、廣、雲、貴者，毋推京營及西北邊，著為令。

translations.literal: An order was issued that from then on commanders arriving from Sichuan, Guangdong, Yunnan, and Guizhou should not be assigned to the capital garrison or the northwestern frontier—this was established as permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The court decreed that hereafter generals coming up from Sichuan, Guangdong, Yunnan, and Guizhou were not to be posted to the capital garrison or the northwest frontier—a rule written into law.

sentences.zh: 從總督張嶽大破賀縣賊倪仲亮等，予實授，仍賚銀幣。

translations.literal: Following Grand Coordinator Zhang Yue he greatly defeated the bandits of Hexian led by Ni Zhongliang and others; he received confirmed appointment and was again granted silver and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Grand Coordinator Zhang Yue, he routed the Hexian bandits led by Ni Zhongliang and others; he received a confirmed commission and another grant of silver and silk.

sentences.zh: 瓊州五指山熟黎素畏法，供徭賦，知州邵浚虐取之。

translations.literal: The acculturated Li of Wuzhi Mountain in Qiongzhou had long feared the law and paid corvée and taxes, but Prefect Shao Jun exploited them cruelly.
translations.idiomatic: The settled Li of Wuzhi Mountain in Qiongzhou had long obeyed the law and paid taxes and corvée, but Prefect Shao Jun preyed on them with brutal exactions.

sentences.zh: 其酋那燕遂結崖州、感恩、昌化諸黎為亂。

translations.literal: Their chieftain Nayang then rallied the Li of Yazhou, Ganan, and Changhua to rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Their chieftain Nayang then joined the Li of Yazhou, Ganan, and Changhua in revolt.

sentences.zh: 總督歐陽必進議並萬州、陵水黎討之，分兵五道。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Ouyang Bijin proposed to subdue them together with the Li of Wanzhou and Lingshui, dividing forces into five columns.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Ouyang Bijin proposed to punish them along with the Li of Wanzhou and Lingshui, dividing the army into five routes.

sentences.zh: 希儀適病，最後至，謂必進曰：「萬州、陵水黎未有黨惡之實，奈何並誅，益樹敵？

translations.literal: Xiyi happened to be ill and arrived last; he told Bijin, "The Li of Wanzhou and Lingshui show no proof of complicity—why punish them together and make more enemies?
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi had fallen ill and arrived last; he told Bijin, "The Li of Wanzhou and Lingshui have done nothing to prove they joined the rebels—why strike them down together and only breed more enemies?

sentences.zh: 莫若止三道。」

translations.literal: Better to halt at three columns.
translations.idiomatic: Better to send only three columns.

sentences.zh: 必進從之。

translations.literal: Bijin agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Bijin took his advice.

sentences.zh: 希儀乃偕參將武鸞、俞大猷等直入五指山下，斬那燕及其黨五千四百有奇，俘獲者五之一，招降三千七百人。

translations.literal: Xiyi then joined vice commanders Wu Luan and Yu Dayou in a direct advance below Wuzhi Mountain, slaying Nayang and more than five thousand four hundred of his followers; one in five were captured, and three thousand seven hundred were persuaded to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi then marched with vice commanders Wu Luan and Yu Dayou straight beneath Wuzhi Mountain, killing Nayang and more than five thousand four hundred of his followers; one-fifth were taken prisoner, and three thousand seven hundred submitted.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，進都督同知，改貴州總兵官。

translations.literal: When victory was reported he was promoted to assistant regional commander and transferred to regional commander of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory arrived, he was promoted to assistant regional commander and reassigned as regional commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 復從嶽平銅仁叛苗龍許保、吳黑苗。

translations.literal: Again following Yue he pacified the rebel Miao Long Xubao and Wu Heimiao of Tongren.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Zhang Yue in pacifying the Tongren rebel Miao Long Xubao and Wu Heimiao.

sentences.zh: 又以病歸。

translations.literal: He returned home once more on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He retired again on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 倭寇海上，命督川、廣兵赴剿。

translations.literal: When Japanese pirates raided the coast he was ordered to lead Sichuan and Guangdong troops to exterminate them.
translations.idiomatic: When Japanese pirates struck the coast, he was ordered to lead Sichuan and Guangdong troops against them.

sentences.zh: 無功，為周如鬥劾罷。

translations.literal: He achieved nothing and was impeached and dismissed by Zhou Rudou.
translations.idiomatic: He accomplished nothing and was impeached and removed by Investigating Censor Zhou Rudou.

sentences.zh: 希儀為人坦率，居恒謔笑，洞見肺腑。

translations.literal: Xiyi was frank by nature; in ordinary times he joked freely, with nothing hidden in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi was open by nature—he joked easily in daily life, and what he felt showed plainly on his face.

sentences.zh: 及臨敵，應變出奇，人莫測。

translations.literal: Yet facing the enemy he adapted with unexpected stratagems no one could fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in battle he shifted with the moment and struck from unexpected angles—no one could read his next move.

sentences.zh: 尤善撫士卒。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at winning over soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Above all he knew how to win soldiers' hearts.

sentences.zh: 常染危病，卒多自戕以禱於神。

translations.literal: When he fell gravely ill, many soldiers maimed themselves to pray to the gods on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When he lay gravely ill, many of his men mutilated themselves in prayer to the gods for his recovery.

sentences.zh: 最後一人，至以箭穿其喉。

translations.literal: The last man went so far as to pierce his own throat with an arrow.
translations.idiomatic: The last of them drove an arrow through his own throat.

sentences.zh: 其得士心如此。

translations.literal: Such was the devotion he commanded.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the hold he had on his men's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 石邦憲，字希尹，貴州清平衛人。

translations.literal: Shi Bangxian, style name Xiyin, was a native of Qingping Guard in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bangxian, styled Xiyin, was a native of Qingping Guard in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖七年嗣世職為指揮使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiajing he inherited his family's hereditary post as commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Jiajing reign he inherited his family's hereditary post as garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 累功，進署都指揮僉事，充銅仁參將。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he was advanced to acting assistant regional commander and served as vice commander of Tongren.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated victories he was promoted to acting assistant regional commander and appointed vice commander of Tongren.

sentences.zh: 苗龍許保、吳黑苗叛，總督張嶽議征之，而賊陷印江、石阡，邦憲坐逮問。

translations.literal: When the Miao Long Xubao and Wu Heimiao rebelled, Grand Coordinator Zhang Yue planned a campaign, but the bandits seized Yinjiang and Shiqian; Bangxian was arrested and investigated for dereliction.
translations.idiomatic: When the Miao Long Xubao and Wu Heimiao rose in rebellion, Grand Coordinator Zhang Yue planned a punitive campaign, but the rebels took Yinjiang and Shiqian, and Bangxian was arrested and brought to account.

sentences.zh: 嶽以銅仁賊巢穴，而邦憲有謀勇，乃奏留之。

translations.literal: Yue reasoned that Tongren was the bandits' lair and Bangxian possessed both strategy and courage, and so memorialized to retain him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue argued that Tongren was the rebels' nest and that Bangxian had both wit and courage, and memorialized to keep him in service.

sentences.zh: 邦憲遂與川、湖兵進貴州，破苗砦十有五。

translations.literal: Bangxian then advanced into Guizhou with troops from Sichuan and Huguang, storming fifteen Miao stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian then marched into Guizhou with Sichuan and Huguang troops and overran fifteen Miao stockades.

sentences.zh: 竄山箐者，搜戮殆盡。

translations.literal: Those who fled into mountain ravines were hunted down nearly to extermination.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fled into the mountain ravines were hunted down almost to the last man.

sentences.zh: 上功，邦憲第一。

translations.literal: When merits were submitted Bangxian ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: When the victory rolls were submitted, Bangxian stood first in merit.

sentences.zh: 未及敘，而許保等突入思州，執知府李允簡以去。

translations.literal: Before rewards were granted, Xubao and others suddenly entered Sizhou and seized Prefect Li Yunjian away.
translations.idiomatic: Before honors could be granted, Xubao and his men burst into Sizhou and carried off Prefect Li Yunjian.

sentences.zh: 邦憲急邀，奪之歸。

translations.literal: Bangxian hurriedly intercepted them and recovered Li.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian raced to intercept them and brought Li back.

sentences.zh: 坐是停俸戴罪。

translations.literal: For this he had his salary suspended while bearing culpability.
translations.idiomatic: For this lapse his pay was suspended and he was ordered to serve under penalty.

sentences.zh: 賊既破思州，復糾余黨，與湖廣蠟爾山苗合，欲攻石阡。

translations.literal: After breaking Sizhou the bandits rallied survivors and joined with the Miaos of La'er Mountain in Huguang, intending to attack Shiqian.
translations.idiomatic: Having overrun Sizhou, the rebels regrouped their remnants and joined the La'er Mountain Miao of Huguang, intending to strike Shiqian.

sentences.zh: 不克，還過省溪。

translations.literal: They failed and withdrew, passing through Xingxi.
translations.idiomatic: They failed in the attempt and withdrew by way of Xingxi.

sentences.zh: 千戶安大朝等邀之，斬獲大半，盡奪其輜重，賊不能軍。

translations.literal: Centurion An Dachao and others ambushed them, killing or capturing more than half and seizing all their baggage trains; the bandits could no longer maintain an army.
translations.idiomatic: Centurion An Dachao and others cut them off, killing or capturing more than half and seizing all their baggage; the rebels could no longer keep an army in the field.

sentences.zh: 邦憲乃使使購老穀、老犭革等執許保送軍門，而黑苗竄如故。

translations.literal: Bangxian then sent envoys to induce Lao Gu, Lao Ge, and others to seize Xubao and deliver him to headquarters, while Heimiao continued to lurk as before.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian then sent agents to bribe Lao Gu, Lao Ge, and others into seizing Xubao and delivering him to headquarters, while Heimiao still lurked in hiding.

sentences.zh: 復以計購烏朗土官田興邦等斬黑苗，賊盡平。

translations.literal: Again by stratagem he induced Tian Xingbang and other native officials of Wulang to behead Heimiao, and the bandits were fully pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Again by stratagem he induced Tian Xingbang and other native officials of Wulang to behead Heimiao, and the rebels were fully subdued.

sentences.zh: 遂進署都督僉事，充總兵官，代沈希儀鎮貴州。

translations.literal: He was then promoted to acting assistant regional commander, appointed regional commander, and replaced Shen Xiyi as garrison commander of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to acting assistant regional commander, appointed regional commander, and replaced Shen Xiyi as commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 臺黎砦苗關保倡亂，四川容山、廣西洪江諸苗應之。

translations.literal: Guanbao of Tailai Stockade Miao incited rebellion, and the Miaos of Rongshan in Sichuan and Hongjiang in Guangxi rose in response.
translations.idiomatic: Guanbao of the Tailai Stockade Miao raised rebellion, and the Miao of Rongshan in Sichuan and Hongjiang in Guangxi answered his call.

sentences.zh: 遠近騷然，撫剿莫能定。

translations.literal: Disturbances spread near and far; neither pacification nor suppression could settle matters.
translations.idiomatic: Alarm spread far and wide, and neither conciliation nor force could restore order.

sentences.zh: 邦憲與湖廣兵分道討破之，傳檄十八砦，許執首惡贖罪。

translations.literal: Bangxian with Huguang troops routed them by separate routes, circulated proclamations to eighteen stockades, and promised amnesty to those who delivered the chief culprits.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian and the Huguang troops broke them on separate routes, issued proclamations to eighteen stockades, and promised pardon to those who handed over the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 諸苗聽撫，設盟受約而還。

translations.literal: The various Miaos submitted to pacification; after establishing oaths and receiving pledges he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao submitted to pacification; after oaths were sworn and pledges received, he withdrew his forces.

sentences.zh: 播州宣慰楊烈殺長官王黼，黼黨李保等治兵相攻且十年，總督馮嶽與邦憲討平之。

translations.literal: Bo Prefectural Commissioner Yang Lie of Bozhou killed Assistant Prefect Wang Fu; Fu's faction under Li Bao and others mustered troops and fought each other for nearly ten years until Grand Coordinator Feng Yue and Bangxian suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Lie, native commissioner of Bozhou, killed Assistant Prefect Wang Fu; Fu's faction under Li Bao and others raised armies and fought for nearly ten years until Grand Coordinator Feng Yue and Bangxian put them down.

sentences.zh: 真州苗盧阿項為亂，邦憲以兵七千編筏渡江，直抵磨子崖。

translations.literal: When the Miao Lu Axian of Zhenzhou rebelled, Bangxian led seven thousand men, lashed rafts to cross the river, and advanced straight to Mozi Cliff.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhenzhou Miao Lu Axian rebelled, Bangxian took seven thousand men, lashed rafts together to cross the river, and marched straight to Mozi Cliff.

sentences.zh: 策賊必夜襲，先設備。

translations.literal: He anticipated a night attack and made preparations beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: He judged the rebels would strike by night and made ready in advance.

sentences.zh: 賊至，擊敗之。

translations.literal: When the bandits came he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When they came, he routed them.

sentences.zh: 賊求援於播州吳鯤。

translations.literal: The bandits sought aid from Wu Kun of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent for help to Wu Kun of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 諸將懼，邦憲曰：「水西宣慰安萬銓，播州所畏也。

translations.literal: The generals were afraid; Bangxian said, "An Wanyin, commissioner of Shuixi native prefecture, is what Bozhou fears.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals were alarmed, but Bangxian said, "An Wanyin, native commissioner of Shuixi, is the man Bozhou dreads.

sentences.zh: 吾調水西兵攻烏江，聲楊烈縱鯤助逆罪，烈奚暇救人乎？」

translations.literal: If I summon Shuixi troops to attack the Wu River and proclaim Yang Lie's crime in abetting Kun's treason, will Lie have leisure to rescue anyone?
translations.idiomatic: If I summon Shuixi troops against the Wu River and proclaim Yang Lie's crime in letting Kun aid rebellion, will Lie have time to save anyone?

sentences.zh: 已，水西兵至。

translations.literal: Before long Shuixi troops arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Shuixi troops arrived.

sentences.zh: 邦憲進逼其巢，乘風縱火，斬關而登，賊大奔潰，擒賊首父子，斬獲四百七十余人。

translations.literal: Bangxian pressed their lair, set fires with the wind at his back, cut through their barriers and scaled the heights; the bandits fled in rout, and the chieftain and his son were captured along with more than four hundred seventy killed or taken.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian pressed their stronghold, set fires with the wind behind him, cut through their barriers and stormed the heights; the rebels broke and fled, the chieftain and his son were captured, and more than four hundred seventy were killed or taken.

sentences.zh: 進署都督同知。

translations.literal: He was promoted to acting assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 破地隆阡叛苗四砦，又破答千諸砦，擒其渠魁。

translations.literal: He stormed four rebel Miao stockades at Dilongqian and also broke the stockades at Daqian, capturing their ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: He overran four rebel Miao stockades at Dilongqian and then broke the stockades at Daqian, capturing their chieftains.

sentences.zh: 地隆阡遺賊龍老三、龍得奎結龍停苗老夭、扳凳苗石章保等縱兵掠，執石耶洞土官妻冉氏以歸，攻梅平砦。

translations.literal: Remnant bandits at Dilongqian—Long Laosan and Long Dekui—joined with Lao Yao of Longting Miao and Shi Zhangbao of Bandeng Miao to raid at will; they seized Lady Ran, wife of the native official of Shiyedong, and attacked Meiping Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Remnant rebels at Dilongqian—Long Laosan and Long Dekui—joined Lao Yao of the Longting Miao and Shi Zhangbao of the Bandeng Miao in raiding at will; they carried off Lady Ran, wife of the native official of Shiyedong, and attacked Meiping Stockade.

sentences.zh: 官軍要擒老三。

translations.literal: Government troops intended to capture Laosan.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops lay in wait to seize Laosan.

sentences.zh: 得奎走免，復與老夭等攻破平南營囤。

translations.literal: Dekui escaped and again with Lao Yao and others breached the depot at Pingnan Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Dekui escaped, then joined Lao Yao and the others in storming the depot at Pingnan Camp.

sentences.zh: 邦憲偵冉氏在老夭所，陽議贖，而潛擊殺老夭。

translations.literal: Bangxian learned Lady Ran was at Lao Yao's camp; he openly negotiated ransom while secretly striking and killing Lao Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian learned Lady Ran was held in Lao Yao's camp; he feigned ransom talks while secretly striking and killing Lao Yao.

sentences.zh: 官軍遂入龍停砦，並執扳凳砦苗龍老內，令執獻章保。

translations.literal: Government troops then entered Longting Stockade and also seized Long Laonei of Bandeng Stockade Miao, ordering him to capture and surrender Zhangbao.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops then entered Longting Stockade and also seized Long Laonei of the Bandeng Miao, ordering him to capture Zhangbao and deliver him up.

sentences.zh: 於是諸苗悉降。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the Miaos submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all the Miao submitted.

sentences.zh: 白洗、養鵝諸苗叛，討擒其魁，降百余砦。

translations.literal: When the Miaos of Baixi and Yang'e rebelled, he suppressed them, captured their chieftains, and received the submission of more than a hundred stockades.
translations.idiomatic: When the Baixi and Yang'e Miao rebelled, he suppressed them, captured their chieftains, and received the surrender of more than a hundred stockades.

sentences.zh: 湖廣漵浦瑤沈亞當等為亂，總督石勇檄邦憲討之，生擒亞當，斬獲二百有奇。

translations.literal: When the Yao Shen Yadang and others of Xupu in Huguang rebelled, Grand Coordinator Shi Yong ordered Bangxian against them; Yadang was captured alive and more than two hundred were killed or taken.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yao Shen Yadang and others of Xupu in Huguang rose in revolt, Grand Coordinator Shi Yong ordered Bangxian against them; Yadang was taken alive and more than two hundred rebels were killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 漵浦甫平，銅仁、都勻苗相煽叛。

translations.literal: Xupu had scarcely been pacified when the Miaos of Tongren and Duyun incited one another to rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Xupu had barely been pacified when the Miao of Tongren and Duyun stirred one another to rebellion.

sentences.zh: 邦憲亟馳還，率守備安大朝進剿。

translations.literal: Bangxian raced back and led garrison commander An Dachao in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian galloped back at once and led Garrison Commander An Dachao in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 先破彪山砦賊，乘勝略定諸砦。

translations.literal: He first broke the bandits of Biaoshan Stockade and, riding the momentum, largely pacified the stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He first broke the rebels at Biaoshan Stockade and, pressing the advantage, largely brought the other stockades to heel.

sentences.zh: 獲賊首龍老羅、王三等，余黨盡平。

translations.literal: Bandit chiefs Long Laoluo and Wang San were captured, and the remaining followers were fully subdued.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel chiefs Long Laoluo and Wang San were captured, and the remaining followers were fully subdued.

sentences.zh: 又與總督黃光升，修湖北墩臺、烽堠百十所，招降冷水溪諸洞苗二十八砦。

translations.literal: Together with Grand Coordinator Huang Guangsheng he repaired more than a hundred and ten beacon towers and signal mounds in Hubei and persuaded twenty-eight stockades of Miaos in the caves of Lengshuixi to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Grand Coordinator Huang Guangsheng he rebuilt more than a hundred and ten signal towers and beacon mounds in Hubei and persuaded twenty-eight Miao stockades in the Lengshuixi caves to submit.

sentences.zh: 播州容山副長官土舍韓甸與正長官土舍張問相攻，甸屢勝，遂糾生苗剽湖、貴境，垂二十年。

translations.literal: Han Dian, deputy assistant prefect of Rongshan in Bozhou, and Zhang Wen, the chief assistant prefect, attacked each other; Dian won repeatedly and then rallied raw Miao to plunder the Huguang and Guizhou borderlands for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Han Dian, deputy native assistant of Rongshan in Bozhou, and Zhang Wen, the chief native assistant, warred against each other; Dian won again and again and then rallied raw Miao to raid the Huguang and Guizhou frontier for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 問亦糾黨自助。

translations.literal: Wen likewise gathered allies to aid himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wen likewise gathered allies of his own.

sentences.zh: 邦憲討之，斬百余人。

translations.literal: Bangxian campaigned against them and killed more than a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian campaigned against them and killed more than a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 問潛出，被獲。

translations.literal: Wen slipped out secretly but was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Wen slipped out in secret but was captured.

sentences.zh: 官軍乘勝入甸巢。

translations.literal: Government troops pressed their advantage into Dian's lair.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops pressed their advantage into Dian's stronghold.

sentences.zh: 會暮，大雨，迷失道。

translations.literal: At dusk a heavy rain fell and they lost their way.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk a torrential rain fell and they lost their way.

sentences.zh: 守備葉勛、百戶魏國相等陷伏中，死焉。

translations.literal: Garrison commander Ye Xun and centurion Wei Guoxiang and others fell into an ambush and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison Commander Ye Xun, Centurion Wei Guoxiang, and others walked into an ambush and were killed.

sentences.zh: 邦憲奪圍出，還軍鎮遠。

translations.literal: Bangxian fought free of the encirclement and withdrew his army to Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian fought his way out of the encirclement and withdrew to Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 再征之，賊沿江守。

translations.literal: On a second campaign the bandits guarded the river line.
translations.idiomatic: On a second campaign the rebels held the river line.

sentences.zh: 邦憲佯與爭，而別自上流三十里編竹以渡。

translations.literal: Bangxian feigned contesting them while separately, thirty li upstream, he lashed bamboo to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian feigned a frontal contest while, thirty li upstream, he lashed bamboo into rafts and crossed.

sentences.zh: 水陸並進，大破之。

translations.literal: Advancing by land and water together, he routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing by land and water together, he broke them completely.

sentences.zh: 斬甸，容山平。

translations.literal: Dian was beheaded and Rongshan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Dian was executed and Rongshan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 進右都督。

translations.literal: He was promoted to right regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right regional commander.

sentences.zh: 邦憲生長黔土，熟苗情。

translations.literal: Bangxian grew up in Qian territory and knew Miao conditions intimately.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian had grown up in Guizhou soil and knew the Miao world inside out.

sentences.zh: 善用兵，大小數十百戰，無不摧破。

translations.literal: Skilled in warfare, through dozens or hundreds of battles large and small he never failed to crush his foes.
translations.idiomatic: He was a master of war; in dozens upon dozens of battles, large and small, he never failed to break his enemy.

sentences.zh: 前後進秩者四，賚銀幣十有三。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced four times in all, and he received silver and silk on thirteen occasions.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was raised four times in all, and he received imperial gifts of silver and silk on thirteen occasions.

sentences.zh: 所得俸賜，悉以饗士，家無贏資。

translations.literal: All salary and gifts he received he spent entirely feasting his soldiers; his household held no surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Every stipend and reward he received he spent entirely on his men; his household kept nothing in reserve.

sentences.zh: 為總兵官十七年，威鎮蠻中。

translations.literal: For seventeen years as regional commander his authority dominated the barbarian lands.
translations.idiomatic: For seventeen years as regional commander his authority held sway over the frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 與四川何卿、廣西沈希儀並稱一時名將。

translations.literal: He was ranked among the age's famous generals together with He Qing of Sichuan and Shen Xiyi of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was counted among the great generals of the age together with He Qing of Sichuan and Shen Xiyi of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 明年卒官。

translations.literal: The next year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈左都督。

translations.literal: He was posthumously ennobled as left regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as left regional commander.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：嗚呼，明至中葉，曷嘗無邊材哉！

translations.literal: The commentator says: Alas! When the Ming reached its middle period, how could it have lacked men of frontier talent!
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Alas—in the Ming dynasty's middle years, when did the empire ever lack men of frontier genius!

sentences.zh: 如馬永、梁震、周尚文、沈希儀之徒，出奇制勝，得士卒死力，雖古名將何以加焉？

translations.literal: Men such as Ma Yong, Liang Zhen, Zhou Shangwen, and Shen Xiyi won by unexpected stratagems, and won soldiers' utter devotion—what ancient famous general could surpass them?
translations.idiomatic: Men like Ma Yong, Liang Zhen, Zhou Shangwen, and Shen Xiyi struck with unexpected stratagems and won their soldiers' utter devotion—what famous general of antiquity could have done more?

sentences.zh: 然功高賞薄，起蹶靡常。

translations.literal: Yet great merit brought thin reward, and their rises and falls were endlessly inconstant.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their deeds outran their rewards, and their fortunes rose and fell without pattern.

sentences.zh: 此無異故，其抗懷奮激，無以結歡在朝柄政重人，宜其齟齬不相入也。

translations.literal: The reason is not hard to find: their proud, impassioned spirits gave them no way to win favor with the heavyweights who held power at court—small wonder they clashed and could not coexist.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is plain: proud and fierce by nature, they had no gift for winning over the powerful men who held the court—and no wonder they grated against one another and against the capital.

sentences.zh: 馬芳三代為將，父子兄弟先後殉國，偉矣哉！

translations.literal: Ma Fang's family produced generals for three generations; father, sons, and brothers one after another died for the state—how magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Ma Fang's house gave the empire generals for three generations—father, sons, and brothers dying for the state one after another. What grandeur!
